sentences.zh: 志六十一

translations.literal: Treatise Sixty-One.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 61.

sentences.zh: 禮五（

translations.literal: Rites Five (
translations.idiomatic: Rites 5 (

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites Five).
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites 5).

sentences.zh: 宗廟之制時饗祫祭加上諡號東西廡配饗醇賢親王廟

translations.literal: Regulations for the ancestral temple; seasonal offerings; collective ancestral sacrifice; posthumous titles; eastern and western side halls for collateral worship; temples for worthy and virtuous princes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestral temple regulations; seasonal sacrifices; joint ancestral rites; bestowal of posthumous titles; collateral worship in the east and west cloisters; temples for worthy and virtuous princes.

sentences.zh: 謁陵

translations.literal: Visiting the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tomb visits.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之制清初尊祀列祖神御，崇德建元，立太廟盛京撫近門東。

translations.literal: As for regulations for the ancestral temple: at the beginning of the Qing, successive ancestors' spirit portraits were honored in worship; when Chongde was established as the reign title, the Imperial Ancestral Temple was erected east of the Fujin Gate in Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: On the regulations governing the imperial ancestral temple: in the early Qing, spirit portraits of successive forebears were venerated; when the Chongde reign was proclaimed, the Imperial Ancestral Temple was built east of the Fujin Gate in Mukden.

sentences.zh: 前殿五室，奉太祖武皇帝、孝慈武皇后。

translations.literal: The front hall had five chambers, enshrining the Martial Emperor Taizu and the Martial Empress Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: The front hall contained five chambers, dedicated to the Martial Emperor Taizu and the Martial Empress Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 後殿三室，奉始祖澤王、高祖慶王、曾祖昌王、祖福王，考、妣俱南鄉。

translations.literal: The rear hall had three chambers, enshrining the Founding Ancestor Prince Ze, the High Ancestor Prince Qing, the Great-Grandfather Prince Chang, and the Grandfather Prince Fu; father and mother both faced south.
translations.idiomatic: The rear hall had three chambers for the Founding Ancestor Prince Ze, the High Ancestor Prince Qing, the Great-Grandfather Prince Chang, and the Grandfather Prince Fu; both father and mother faced south.

sentences.zh: 並設床榻、衾枕、楎椸、帷幔，如生事儀。

translations.literal: Beds, quilts, pillows, clothes racks, and curtains were also set out, as in the rites for attending to the living.
translations.idiomatic: Beds, bedding, pillows, garment racks, and curtains were also provided, following the ceremonial provisions for attending to the living.

sentences.zh: 太宗受尊號，躬率群臣祭告，其太牢、少牢色尚黑。

translations.literal: When Taizong received his honorific title, he personally led the ministers in offering sacrifice and announcement; for the great and lesser offerings, black was the preferred color.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong received his honorific title, he personally led the ministers in sacrificial announcement; for the major and minor offerings, black was the prescribed color.

sentences.zh: 復嗣考祭儀，定祭品，牛一，羊一，豕一，簠、簋各二，籩、豆各十有二，爐一，鐙二，各帛一，登、鉶、尊各一，玉爵三，金匕一，金箸二。

translations.literal: The sacrificial rites for the deceased father were restored; sacrificial offerings were fixed as one ox, one sheep, one pig, two gui and two fu vessels each, twelve baskets and twelve dou vessels each, one censer, two lamps, one bolt of silk each, one deng, one xing, and one zun each, three jade goblets, one gold spoon, and two gold chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: The rites for sacrificing to the deceased father were restored, and the offerings were fixed: one ox, one sheep, one pig; two fu and two gui vessels; twelve baskets and twelve dou vessels; one censer and two lamps, each with one bolt of silk; one deng, one xing, and one zun; three jade goblets; one gold spoon; and two gold chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 帛共篚，牲共俎。

translations.literal: Silks shared one basket; victims shared one tray.
translations.idiomatic: Silks were placed together in one basket; sacrificial animals on one tray.

sentences.zh: 尊實酒，疏布冪勺具。

translations.literal: The zun was filled with wine; coarse-cloth covers and ladles were provided.
translations.idiomatic: The wine vessel was filled; coarse-cloth covers and ladles were set out.

sentences.zh: 階前設樂部，分左、右懸。

translations.literal: A music corps was set before the steps, divided into left and right suspended sets.
translations.idiomatic: A musical ensemble was stationed before the steps, with left and right suspended orchestras.

sentences.zh: 祀日陳法駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the imperial procession regalia was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, the imperial procession and guard of honor were arrayed.

sentences.zh: 世祖定燕京，建太廟端門左，南鄉。

translations.literal: When Shizu fixed the capital at Yanjing, he built the Imperial Ancestral Temple to the left of the Duan Gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu established the capital at Beijing, he built the Imperial Ancestral Temple to the left of the Duan Gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 硃門丹壁，上覆黃琉璃，衛以崇垣，周二百九十一丈。

translations.literal: Vermilion gates and cinnabar walls, roofed above with yellow glazed tiles, guarded by a lofty enclosure wall, with a perimeter of two hundred ninety-one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: It had vermilion gates and cinnabar walls, a roof of yellow glazed tiles, and a high enclosing wall measuring two hundred ninety-one zhang in circumference.

sentences.zh: 凡殿三，前殿十一楹，階三成，陛皆五齣。

translations.literal: In all there were three halls; the front hall had eleven bays, with three tiers of steps, each flight having five treads.
translations.idiomatic: There were three halls in all: the front hall had eleven bays, three tiers of steps, and five treads on each flight.

sentences.zh: 一成四級，二成五級，三成中十一，左、右各九。

translations.literal: The first tier had four steps, the second five, and the third tier had eleven in the center and nine each on the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The first tier had four steps, the second five, and the third tier eleven steps in the center and nine on each side.

sentences.zh: 中奉太祖、太后神龕。

translations.literal: In the center were enshrined the spirit shrines of Taizu and the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The center enshrined the spirit shrines of Taizu and the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 中殿九楹，同堂異室，奉列聖、列後神龕。

translations.literal: The middle hall had nine bays, one hall with separate chambers, enshrining the spirit shrines of successive emperors and empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The middle hall had nine bays under one roof but with separate chambers, housing the spirit shrines of successive emperors and empresses.

sentences.zh: 後界硃垣，中三門，左、右各一。

translations.literal: Behind was bounded a vermilion wall, with three gates in the center and one each on the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: To the rear stood a vermilion enclosure with three central gates and one each on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 為後殿，亦九楹，奉祧廟神龕，俱南鄉。

translations.literal: This served as the rear hall, also of nine bays, enshrining the spirit shrines of the distant-ancestor temple; all faced south.
translations.idiomatic: This was the rear hall, likewise of nine bays, enshrining the distant-ancestor spirit shrines, all facing south.

sentences.zh: 前殿兩廡各十五楹，東諸王配饗，西功臣配饗。

translations.literal: The two side cloisters of the front hall each had fifteen bays; on the east, princes received collateral worship, on the west, meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Each side cloister of the front hall had fifteen bays: princes were worshipped collaterally on the east, meritorious ministers on the west.

sentences.zh: 東廡前、西廡南燎爐各一。

translations.literal: One brazier each was placed at the front of the east cloister and the south of the west cloister.
translations.idiomatic: There was one brazier at the front of the east cloister and one at the south end of the west cloister.

sentences.zh: 中後殿兩廡庋祭器。

translations.literal: The two cloisters of the middle and rear halls stored sacrificial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The side cloisters of the middle and rear halls stored the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 東廡南燎爐一。

translations.literal: One brazier at the south of the east cloister.
translations.idiomatic: There was one brazier at the south end of the east cloister.

sentences.zh: 戟門五，中三門內外列戟百二十，左、右門各三。

translations.literal: There were five halberd gates; within and without the three central gates, one hundred twenty halberds were arrayed; the left and right gates each had three.
translations.idiomatic: There were five halberd gates; one hundred twenty halberds were displayed inside and outside the three central gates, and three at each of the side gates.

sentences.zh: 其外石樑五。

translations.literal: Outside were five stone bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Outside stood five stone bridges.

sentences.zh: 橋北井亭三，南神庫、神廚。

translations.literal: North of the bridges were three well pavilions; to the south, the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: North of the bridges were three well pavilions; to the south were the spirit storehouse and spirit kitchen.

sentences.zh: 西南奉祀署，東南宰牲亭。

translations.literal: To the southwest was the Sacrificial Service Office; to the southeast, the slaughter pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Service Office stood to the southwest, and the slaughter pavilion to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 其盛京太廟尊為四祖廟雲。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple at Mukden was honored as the Temple of the Four Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple at Mukden was revered as the Temple of the Four Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，定盛京守廟首領馬法秩視拖沙喇哈番，餘馬法視護軍校。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, it was fixed that the chief mafa who guarded the Mukden temple should rank equal to a tosahala hafan, and the other mafa equal to a garrison banner officer.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4, the chief mafa in charge of the Mukden temple was given rank equivalent to a tosahala hafan, and the other mafa to a garrison banner officer.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，追尊澤王為肇祖，慶王為興祖，昌王為景祖，福王為顯祖，與四後並奉後殿，致祭如時饗儀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year, Prince Ze was posthumously honored as the Founding Ancestor, Prince Qing as the Rising Ancestor, Prince Chang as the Illustrious Ancestor, and Prince Fu as the Manifest Ancestor; together with the four consorts they were all enshrined in the rear hall, and sacrifice was performed according to the seasonal offering rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year, Prince Ze was posthumously elevated as the Founding Ancestor, Prince Qing as the Rising Ancestor, Prince Chang as the Illustrious Ancestor, and Prince Fu as the Manifest Ancestor; with their four consorts they were all installed in the rear hall and worshipped according to the seasonal offering rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，孝端文皇后祔廟，奉神主祗見太祖、太后暨太宗，代行三跪九拜禮，位次太宗，復一跪三拜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Empress Xiaoduanwen was enshrined in the temple; bearing the spirit tablet, she was presented before Taizu, the Empress Dowager, and Taizong; on her behalf the three kneelings and nine prostrations were performed; her place was next after Taizong, followed by one kneeling and three prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Empress Xiaoduanwen was installed in the ancestral temple; her spirit tablet was presented before Taizu, the Empress Dowager, and Taizong, with the three kneelings and nine prostrations performed on her behalf; her position was next after Taizong, followed by one kneeling and three prostrations.

sentences.zh: 畢，遂行大饗。

translations.literal: When this was completed, the great communal feast was then performed.
translations.idiomatic: When this was done, the great communal feast followed.

sentences.zh: 祀後殿則遣官。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the rear hall was performed by dispatched officials.
translations.idiomatic: Worship at the rear hall was carried out by dispatched officials.

sentences.zh: 凡升祔，先一日遣告，至日祗見、奉安、大饗，著為例。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an elevation and enshrinement, announcement was dispatched one day beforehand; on the day itself, presentation, installation, and the great feast were performed—this was established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For every elevation and enshrinement, announcement was sent one day in advance; on the appointed day came presentation, installation, and the great feast—this became the established precedent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，世祖祔廟，位次太祖西旁，東鄉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Shizu was enshrined in the temple, his place to the west of Taizu, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Shizu was installed in the temple, placed to the west of Taizu and facing east.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，孝康章皇后祔廟，位次世祖。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, Empress Xiaokangzhang was enshrined in the temple, her place next after Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9, Empress Xiaokangzhang was installed in the temple, placed next after Shizu.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，孝庄文皇后祔廟，屆期世祖及章後神主避立於旁，始行祗見禮，位次文後。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Xiaozhuangwen was enshrined in the temple; when the day arrived, the spirit tablets of Shizu and Empress Zhang were moved aside to stand at the side, and only then was the presentation rite performed; her place was next after Empress Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Xiaozhuangwen was installed in the temple; on the appointed day the spirit tablets of Shizu and Empress Zhang were set aside before the presentation rite was performed; her position was next after Empress Wen.

sentences.zh: 凡祔廟主，以卑避尊，後仿此。

translations.literal: Whenever spirit tablets were enshrined in the temple, the inferior yielded to the superior; later cases followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tablets were installed in the temple, the junior yielded place to the senior; later cases followed this precedent.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，孝惠章皇后升祔，議者以孝康祔廟久，欲位其次。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, Empress Xiaohuizhang was elevated for enshrinement; some in the deliberations, noting that Empress Xiaokang had long been enshrined, wished to place her next in order.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year, Empress Xiaohuizhang was elevated for enshrinement; some argued that because Empress Xiaokang had been installed long before, Xiaohui should be placed immediately after her.

sentences.zh: 大學士王掞議曰：「陛下聖孝格天，曩時太皇太后祔廟，不以躋孝端上，今肯以孝康躋孝惠上乎？」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Yan memorialized: "Your Majesty's sagely filial piety moves Heaven; in former times, when the Grand Empress Dowager was enshrined, she was not placed above Xiaoduan—would Your Majesty now place Xiaokang above Xiaohui?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Yan argued: "Your Majesty's filial devotion moves Heaven; when the Grand Empress Dowager was installed, she was not ranked above Xiaoduan—would Your Majesty now rank Xiaokang above Xiaohui?"

sentences.zh: 議者不從，帝果以為非是，令改正焉。

translations.literal: The deliberators did not follow this, but the Emperor indeed held it incorrect and ordered the arrangement corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberators did not accept this, but the Emperor indeed judged it wrong and ordered the placement corrected.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，禮臣言：「古帝王升祔太廟，必以皇后配饗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the ritual officials said: "When ancient emperors were elevated and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, an empress was invariably joined in collateral worship.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, the ritual officials stated: "When ancient emperors were installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, an empress was always joined in collateral worship.

sentences.zh: 周祀閟宮，漢於別寢，唐、宋有坤儀、奉慈殿以展孝思。

translations.literal: The Zhou worshipped at the Bicong Palace, the Han at separate chambers, and the Tang and Song had the Kunyi and Fengci halls to express filial remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou worshipped at the Bicong Palace, the Han in separate chambers, and the Tang and Song had the Kunyi and Fengci halls to express filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 自是配廟者，皇后字上一字與廟諡同，祀別廟者，但有諡無廟號。

translations.literal: From this, for those joined in the main temple, the first character of the empress's title matched the temple posthumous name; for those worshipped in separate temples, there was only a posthumous title and no temple name.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for empresses joined in the main temple, the first character of their title matched the temple posthumous name; for those worshipped in separate temples, there was only a posthumous title and no temple name.

sentences.zh: 其配位或一帝一後，或一帝二後。

translations.literal: As for collateral places, there might be one emperor and one empress, or one emperor and two empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral placement might be one emperor with one empress, or one emperor with two empresses.

sentences.zh: 宋太宗、徽宗則四後先後升祔，禮制不同。

translations.literal: Under Song Taizong and Song Huizong, four empresses were in turn elevated and enshrined—the ritual systems differed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Taizong and Huizong, four empresses were installed in succession—the ritual systems differed.

sentences.zh: 本朝太祖三後，唯孝慈祔廟稱高後，太宗二後，孝端、孝庄並稱文後，世祖三後，孝惠、孝康並稱章後，孝獻但祀孝陵饗殿，定制然也。

translations.literal: In our dynasty Taizu had three empresses, but only Xiaoci, enshrined in the temple, was styled the High Empress; Taizong had two empresses, Xiaoduan and Xiaozhuang both styled the Wen Empress; Shizu had three empresses, Xiaohui and Xiaokang both styled the Zhang Empress, while Xiaoxian was worshipped only at the feast hall of the Xiaoling tomb—such was the established regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty Taizu had three empresses, but only Xiaoci, installed in the temple, was styled the High Empress; Taizong had two empresses, Xiaoduan and Xiaozhuang, both styled the Wen Empress; Shizu had three empresses, Xiaohui and Xiaokang both styled the Zhang Empress, while Xiaoxian was worshipped only at the Xiaoling feast hall—such was the established regulation.

sentences.zh: 今聖祖祔廟，仁孝作配，允宜同饗。

translations.literal: Now that the Sage Ancestor is enshrined in the temple, Renxiao should serve as his collateral partner—it is altogether fitting that they share the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Sage Ancestor is installed in the temple, Renxiao should serve as his collateral partner, and it is altogether fitting that they share the feast.

sentences.zh: 第廟諡曰仁，與尊諡複，改題孝誠，與孝恭體備母儀，並宜同祔。

translations.literal: Only the temple posthumous name Ren duplicated the honorific title; it was changed to Xiaocheng; together with Xiaogong, who fully embodied the model of motherhood, both should likewise be enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Only the temple posthumous name Ren duplicated the honorific title, so it was changed to Xiaocheng; together with Xiaogong, who fully embodied the model of motherhood, both should likewise be installed.

sentences.zh: 其孝昭、孝懿，應集廷臣詳議。」

translations.literal: As for Xiaozhao and Xiaoyi, court ministers should be assembled for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: As for Xiaozhao and Xiaoyi, court ministers should be assembled for detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 尋議定：「夏、商逮六朝，皆一帝一後，唐睿宗二後，宋太祖三後，太宗四後。

translations.literal: Soon it was deliberated and fixed: "From Xia and Shang through the Six Dynasties, all had one emperor and one empress; Tang Ruizong had two empresses, Song Taizu three, and Song Taizong four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was decided: "From Xia and Shang through the Six Dynasties, all had one emperor and one empress; Tang Ruizong had two empresses, Song Taizu three, and Song Taizong four.

sentences.zh: 祔廟之制，硃子諸儒咸無異說。

translations.literal: On the regulations for enshrinement in the temple, the Zhu Xi school of scholars were all of one opinion.
translations.idiomatic: On the regulations for temple enshrinement, the Zhu Xi school of scholars were unanimous.

sentences.zh: 謹按前典，孝昭、孝懿應與孝誠、孝恭並稱仁皇后，同祔太廟。」

translations.literal: Respectfully examining former statutes, Xiaozhao and Xiaoyi should together with Xiaocheng and Xiaogong all be styled Ren Empress and jointly enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining former statutes, Xiaozhao and Xiaoyi should, together with Xiaocheng and Xiaogong, all be styled Ren Empress and jointly installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 案儀，一元後，一繼立，一本生，並列如序。

translations.literal: According to the rites, one primary empress, one successor empress, and one birth mother were all arranged in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: According to the rites, one primary empress, one successor empress, and one birth mother were all arranged in proper order.

sentences.zh: 首孝誠，次孝昭，次孝懿，次孝恭。

translations.literal: First Xiaocheng, then Xiaozhao, then Xiaoyi, then Xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: First came Xiaocheng, then Xiaozhao, then Xiaoyi, then Xiaogong.

sentences.zh: 於此奉帝、後神主，以次安東旁，西鄉，位次太宗。

translations.literal: Here the spirit tablets of emperor and empresses were borne and installed in order on the east side, facing west, their places next after Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: There the spirit tablets of the emperor and empresses were borne and installed in order on the east side, facing west, next after Taizong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，世宗暨孝敬後祔廟，位西旁，東鄉，居世祖次。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Shizong and Empress Xiaojing were enshrined in the temple, their places on the west side facing east, ranking next after Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2, Shizong and Empress Xiaojing were installed in the temple on the west side facing east, ranking next after Shizu.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，孝聖后升祔，次孝敬。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, Empress Xiaosheng was elevated for enshrinement, next after Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, Empress Xiaosheng was elevated for enshrinement, placed next after Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 明年，高宗詣盛京，徙建四祖廟大清門東，南北袤十一丈一尺五寸，東西廣十丈三尺五寸。

translations.literal: The following year, Gaozong went to Mukden and relocated and rebuilt the Temple of the Four Ancestors east of the Daqing Gate, measuring eleven zhang one chi five cun north to south and ten zhang three chi five cun east to west.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Gaozong went to Mukden and rebuilt the Temple of the Four Ancestors east of the Daqing Gate, measuring eleven zhang one chi five cun from north to south and ten zhang three chi five cun from east to west.

sentences.zh: 正殿五楹，東、西配廡各三楹。

translations.literal: The main hall had five bays; the eastern and western side halls each had three bays.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had five bays, with three-bay side halls on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 正門三，東、西門各一。

translations.literal: There were three main gates and one each on the east and west.
translations.idiomatic: There were three main gates and one each on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 敕大臣監視落成。

translations.literal: An edict ordered grand ministers to supervise completion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered senior ministers to supervise the completion of construction.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，高宗暨孝賢、孝儀二後祔廟，位東旁，西鄉，次聖祖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, Gaozong together with Empresses Xiaoxian and Xiaoyi were enshrined in the temple, their places on the east side facing west, next after the Sage Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, Gaozong together with Empresses Xiaoxian and Xiaoyi were installed in the temple on the east side facing west, next after the Sage Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，仁宗暨孝淑後祔廟，位西序，東鄉，次世宗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, Renzong together with Empress Xiaoshu were enshrined in the temple, their places in the western row facing east, next after Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1, Renzong together with Empress Xiaoshu were installed in the temple in the western row facing east, next after Shizong.

sentences.zh: 三十年，宣宗遺諭及祔廟事，略謂：「禮經天子七廟，周禮小宗伯辨廟祧昭穆，漢七廟六室，唐九代十一室，宋九世十二室，議禮紛紛，不一而足。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, in his testamentary instruction on enshrinement in the temple, Xuanzong said in summary: "The Rites Classic speaks of seven temples for the Son of Heaven; the Zhou Rites' Lesser Minister of Ancestral Affairs distinguished temple, distant-ancestor, zhao, and mu lines; the Han had seven temples and six chambers, the Tang nine generations and eleven chambers, the Song nine generations and twelve chambers—deliberations on ritual were numerous and not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, in his testamentary instruction on temple enshrinement, Xuanzong stated in summary: "The Rites Classic speaks of seven temples for the Son of Heaven; the Zhou Rites' Lesser Minister of Ancestral Affairs distinguished temple lines, distant ancestors, and zhao and mu positions; the Han had seven temples and six chambers, the Tang nine generations and eleven chambers, the Song nine generations and twelve chambers—ritual deliberations were numerous and inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 我朝首太祖訖仁宗，巍然七室，不參酌今古，必至貽笑後嗣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty from Taizu down to Renzong already has seven chambers standing in majesty; if we do not weigh past and present, we will surely invite the ridicule of later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty from Taizu down to Renzong already has seven chambers standing in majesty; if we do not weigh past and present practice, we will surely invite ridicule from later generations.

sentences.zh: 朕薄德承基，何敢上擬祖考，祔廟斷不可行。

translations.literal: I, of slight virtue inheriting the foundation, how dare I rank myself with ancestors and forebears—enshrinement in the temple is absolutely not to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: I, of slight virtue inheriting the foundation, how dare I rank myself with my ancestors—installation in the temple must absolutely not proceed.

sentences.zh: 其奉先殿、壽皇殿、安佑宮為古原廟，制可仍舊。」

translations.literal: The Fengxian Hall, Shouhuang Hall, and Anyou Palace serve as the ancient separate temples; their regulations may remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: The Fengxian Hall, Shouhuang Hall, and Anyou Palace serve as the ancient separate temples, and their regulations may remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 乃下廷臣議，於是禮親王全齡等主遵成憲。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued for court ministers to deliberate; thereupon Prince Li Quanling and others upheld adherence to established statutes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued for court ministers to deliberate; thereupon Prince Li Quanling and others upheld adherence to established statutes.

sentences.zh: 侍郎曾國籓亦言：「萬難遵從。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zeng Guofan also said: "It would be exceedingly difficult to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zeng Guofan also argued: "It would be exceedingly difficult to follow this instruction.

sentences.zh: 古者祧廟，為七廟親盡言，有親盡不祧者，則必世德作求，不在七廟數。

translations.literal: In antiquity, the distant-ancestor temple spoke of the seven temples when kinship was exhausted; where kinship was exhausted yet removal did not occur, there must have been generations of virtue calling forth blessing—they were not counted within the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, the distant-ancestor temple concerned the seven temples when kinship was exhausted; where kinship was exhausted yet removal did not occur, there must have been generations of accumulated virtue—they were not counted within the seven temples.

sentences.zh: 若殷三宗，周文、武是也。

translations.literal: Such were the Three Ancestors of Yin and Wen and Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the Three Ancestors of Yin and King Wen and King Wu of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝於皇上為禰廟，非七廟親盡比，而功德彌綸，又當與列祖、列宗同為百世不祧之室。

translations.literal: The late emperor, for Your Majesty, is the temple of the father—this is not comparable to the exhaustion of kinship in the seven temples, yet his merit and virtue fill the realm; he should likewise share with successive ancestors and forebears a chamber never removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, for Your Majesty, is the temple of the father—this is not comparable to the exhaustion of kinship in the seven temples, yet his merit and virtue fill the realm; he should likewise share with successive ancestors and forebears a chamber never removed for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 且諸侯大夫尚有廟祭，況尊如天子，敢廢祔典？」

translations.literal: Moreover, even feudal lords and grand masters still had temple sacrifice—how much more one honored as the Son of Heaven: dare we abolish the rite of enshrinement?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even feudal lords and grandees still had temple sacrifice—how much more one honored as the Son of Heaven: dare we abolish the rite of enshrinement?"

sentences.zh: 帝俞其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「天子七廟，特禮之常制，非合不祧之室言也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Son of Heaven's seven temples are merely the ordinary regulation of ritual—they do not speak of chambers joined and never removed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The Son of Heaven's seven temples are merely the ordinary regulation of ritual—they do not speak of chambers joined and never removed.

sentences.zh: 皇考祔廟稱宗，於制為允。」

translations.literal: Enshrining the Imperial Father in the temple and styling him Zong is permissible within the regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Installing the Imperial Father in the temple and styling him Zong is permissible within the regulations."

sentences.zh: 遂於咸豐二年，奉宣宗暨孝穆、孝慎、孝全三後祔廟，位東序，西鄉，次高宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the second year of Xianfeng, Xuanzong together with Empresses Xiaomu, Xiaoshen, and Xiaquan were enshrined in the temple, their places in the eastern row facing west, next after Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon in Xianfeng 2, Xuanzong together with Empresses Xiaomu, Xiaoshen, and Xiaquan were installed in the temple in the eastern row facing west, next after Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 明年，奉孝和睿皇后升祔，次孝淑。

translations.literal: The following year, Empress Xiahe Rui was elevated for enshrinement, next after Xiaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Empress Xiahe Rui was elevated for enshrinement, placed next after Xiaoshu.

sentences.zh: 文宗少時為康慈太后撫育，十一年帝崩，穆宗體大行遺志，上尊諡曰孝靜。

translations.literal: In his youth Wenzong was reared by Empress Dowager Kangci; in the eleventh year the Emperor died, and Muzong, following the late emperor's testamentary wish, bestowed the honorific posthumous title Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wenzong was reared by Empress Dowager Kangci; in the eleventh year the Emperor died, and Muzong, following the late emperor's testamentary wish, bestowed the honorific posthumous title Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 同治建元，祔廟次孝全。

translations.literal: When the Tongzhi reign was inaugurated, she was enshrined in the temple next after Xiaquan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi reign was inaugurated, she was installed in the temple next after Xiaquan.

sentences.zh: 四年，文宗暨孝德後祔廟，位西序，東鄉，次仁宗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wenzong together with Empress Xiaode were enshrined in the temple, their places in the western row facing east, next after Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wenzong together with Empress Xiaode were installed in the temple in the western row facing east, next after Renzong.

sentences.zh: 於時太廟中殿，九楹咸序。

translations.literal: At that time in the middle hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, all nine bays were fully ordered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all nine bays of the middle hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were fully occupied.

sentences.zh: 洎穆宗崩御，而祔次尚虛。

translations.literal: When Muzong died, the place for enshrinement was still vacant.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong died, the place for enshrinement remained vacant.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，惇親王奕脤等躬往相度，集議所宜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, Prince Dun Yizun and others personally went to survey the site and assembled deliberations on what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3, Prince Dun Yizun and others personally surveyed the site and assembled deliberations on what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 侍講張佩綸請仿殷、周制，立太宗世室，百世不祧。

translations.literal: Hanlin Lecturer Zhang Peilun requested that, following the institutions of Yin and Zhou, a Shizong lineage chamber be established, never removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Lecturer Zhang Peilun proposed that, following the institutions of Yin and Zhou, a Taizong lineage chamber be established, never removed for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 展後殿旁垣左右各建世室。

translations.literal: Extend the side walls beside the rear hall and build lineage chambers on the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Extend the side walls beside the rear hall and build lineage chambers on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 侍郎袁保恆謂周制世室在太祖廟旁，居昭穆上，後世同堂異室，以近祖為尊。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yuan Baoheng said that in the Zhou system the lineage chamber stood beside the temple of the Great Ancestor, ranking above zhao and mu; in later ages one hall with separate chambers honored the nearer ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yuan Baoheng argued that in the Zhou system the lineage chamber stood beside the temple of the Great Ancestor, ranking above zhao and mu; in later ages one hall with separate chambers honored the nearer ancestor.

sentences.zh: 請以中殿太祖左右為世室九楹，東西各展兩楹，別建昭穆六代親廟。

translations.literal: He requested that to the left and right of Taizu in the middle hall there be lineage chambers of nine bays, extending two bays each to east and west, and separately building zhao and mu temples for six generations of close kin.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that to the left and right of Taizu in the middle hall there be nine-bay lineage chambers, extending two bays each to east and west, and separately building zhao and mu temples for six generations of close kin.

sentences.zh: 太祖居中，兩旁各六楹，為左右世室。

translations.literal: Taizu would be centered, with six bays on each side serving as the left and right lineage chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu would be centered, with six bays on each side serving as the left and right lineage chambers.

sentences.zh: 太祖至穆宗同為百世不祧，不必俟親盡遞升。

translations.literal: From Taizu down to Muzong would alike be never removed for a hundred generations, without waiting for kinship exhaustion and successive elevation.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu down to Muzong would alike be never removed for a hundred generations, without waiting for kinship exhaustion and successive elevation.

sentences.zh: 其左右隙地，更建兩廟，各三楹，為三昭三穆，循次繼入，藉省遷移。

translations.literal: On the vacant ground to left and right, two more temples would be built, each of three bays, for three zhao and three mu, entering in succession by order, thereby saving removals.
translations.idiomatic: On the vacant ground to left and right, two more temples would be built, each of three bays, for three zhao and three mu, entering in succession by order, thereby avoiding repeated removals.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺卿徐樹銘言：「古者廟前寢後，廟以祭饗，今前殿是；

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Xu Shuming said: "In antiquity the temple was in front and the sleeping chamber behind; the temple was for sacrificial feasting—the present front hall is this;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Xu Shuming argued: "In antiquity the temple was in front and the sleeping chamber behind; the temple was for sacrificial feasting—the present front hall serves this purpose;

sentences.zh: 寢以藏衣冠，今中殿、後殿是。

translations.literal: the sleeping chamber was for storing robes and caps—the present middle and rear halls are this.
translations.idiomatic: the sleeping chamber was for storing robes and caps—the present middle and rear halls serve this purpose.

sentences.zh: 茲所當議者，藏衣冠寢殿耳。

translations.literal: What should now be deliberated is only the sleeping chamber for storing robes and caps.
translations.idiomatic: What should now be deliberated is only the sleeping chamber for storing robes and caps.

sentences.zh: 應就中殿左建寢殿，祭饗仍在前殿。

translations.literal: A sleeping hall should be built to the left of the middle hall, while sacrificial feasting would remain in the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: A sleeping hall should be built to the left of the middle hall, while sacrificial feasts would continue in the front hall.

sentences.zh: 列祖、列宗，百世不祧，若建世室後殿旁，反嫌居太祖上。

translations.literal: Successive ancestors and forebears, never removed for a hundred generations—if lineage chambers were built beside the rear hall, it would seem to place them above Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Successive ancestors and forebears were never to be removed for a hundred generations; building lineage chambers beside the rear hall would seem to rank them above Taizu.

sentences.zh: 唯增寢室，則昭穆序矣。」

translations.literal: Only by adding sleeping chambers would the zhao and mu order be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Only by adding sleeping chambers would the zhao and mu order be preserved."

sentences.zh: 其他條議，大率主世室者多。

translations.literal: Other proposals mostly favored lineage chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Other proposals mostly favored establishing lineage chambers.

sentences.zh: 有謂後殿宜增殿宇，移四祖神主其中。

translations.literal: Some said the rear hall should be enlarged and the spirit tablets of the Four Ancestors moved there.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the rear hall should be enlarged and the spirit tablets of the Four Ancestors moved there.

sentences.zh: 改為世室，移太宗居中一室。

translations.literal: It should be converted into a lineage chamber, with Taizong moved to the central chamber.
translations.idiomatic: It should be converted into a lineage chamber, with Taizong moved to the central chamber.

sentences.zh: 穆宗祔廟，奉安中殿西第四室者，通政使錫珍說也。

translations.literal: That Muzong's enshrinement should install him in the fourth western chamber of the middle hall was the proposal of Censor-in-Chief Xi Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal that Muzong be installed in the fourth western chamber of the middle hall came from Censor-in-Chief Xi Zhen.

sentences.zh: 有謂中殿兩旁建世室，東二西一，中奉太祖主，七廟東一廟奉太宗，二廟奉聖祖；

translations.literal: Some said lineage chambers should be built on both sides of the middle hall, two on the east and one on the west; in the center Taizu's tablet would be worshipped; of the seven temples, one eastern temple would worship Taizong and two temples the Sage Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed lineage chambers on both sides of the middle hall, two on the east and one on the west; Taizu would be worshipped in the center; of the seven temples, one eastern temple would house Taizong and two the Sage Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 西一廟奉世祖。

translations.literal: one western temple would worship Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: and one western temple would house Shizu.

sentences.zh: 前殿兩旁建六親廟，世宗以下奉之，斯昭穆不紊。

translations.literal: Six temples for close kin would be built on both sides of the front hall, worshipping Shizong and those below—thus zhao and mu would not be disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Six temples for close kin would be built on both sides of the front hall for Shizong and his successors—thus preserving proper zhao and mu order.

sentences.zh: 少詹事文治說也。

translations.literal: This was the proposal of Junior Guardian Wen Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the proposal of Junior Guardian Wen Zhi.

sentences.zh: 有謂中殿兩旁建昭穆二世室，但建方殿，縱橫各五楹，移太宗居昭世室，世祖居穆世室，皆北面中一楹。

translations.literal: Some said zhao and mu lineage chambers should be built on both sides of the middle hall, erecting only square halls of five bays each in length and breadth; Taizong would be moved to the zhao lineage chamber, Shizu to the mu lineage chamber, each facing north in the central bay.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed zhao and mu lineage chambers on both sides of the middle hall, square halls of five bays in each dimension; Taizong would move to the zhao lineage chamber and Shizu to the mu, each facing north from the central bay.

sentences.zh: 聖祖居昭世室，東面第一楹。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor would occupy the zhao lineage chamber, in the first eastern bay.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Ancestor would occupy the zhao lineage chamber in the first eastern bay.

sentences.zh: 中殿仍奉太祖。

translations.literal: The middle hall would still worship Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The middle hall would continue to enshrine Taizu.

sentences.zh: 昭穆各四楹，列聖神位依序上移。

translations.literal: Zhao and mu would each have four bays; the spirit places of successive emperors would be shifted upward in order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and mu would each have four bays, with successive emperors' spirit places shifted upward in order.

sentences.zh: 穆宗升祔，居昭第三楹。

translations.literal: When Muzong was elevated for enshrinement, he would occupy the third zhao bay.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong was elevated for enshrinement, he would occupy the third zhao bay.

sentences.zh: 司業寶廷說也。

translations.literal: This was the proposal of Director of Studies Bao Ting.
translations.idiomatic: This was the proposal of Director of Studies Bao Ting.

sentences.zh: 已，閣議以紛更廟制，未可從。

translations.literal: In the end, the Grand Council deliberated that because the temple system would be repeatedly altered, this could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, the Grand Council held that repeatedly altering the temple system made these proposals unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 禮親王世鐸等謂：「與其附會古典，不如恪守成規。

translations.literal: Prince Li Shiduo and others said: "Rather than forcing conformity with ancient models, it is better to adhere to established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Shiduo and others argued: "Rather than forcing conformity with ancient models, it is better to adhere to established regulations.

sentences.zh: 太廟中殿九楹，中楹仍舊，東西各四楹，請如道光初故事，增修改飾。

translations.literal: The middle hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple has nine bays; the central bay remains as before, with four bays each to east and west; we request following the precedent of the early Daoguang period to enlarge, alter, and refurbish.
translations.idiomatic: The middle hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple has nine bays, with the central bay unchanged and four on each side; we request following the early Daoguang precedent to enlarge and refurbish it.

sentences.zh: 東次楹又次楹為昭位，太宗暨二後、聖祖暨四後、高宗暨二後、宣宗暨四後神主序焉。

translations.literal: The second and third eastern bays would be zhao positions, ordering the spirit tablets of Taizong with two empresses, the Sage Ancestor with four empresses, Gaozong with two empresses, and Xuanzong with four empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The second and third eastern bays would be zhao positions, ordering the spirit tablets of Taizong with two empresses, the Sage Ancestor with four, Gaozong with two, and Xuanzong with four.

sentences.zh: 西次楹又次楹為穆位，世祖暨二後、世宗暨二後、仁宗暨二後、文宗、孝德後神主序焉。

translations.literal: The second and third western bays would be mu positions, ordering the spirit tablets of Shizu with two empresses, Shizong with two empresses, Renzong with two empresses, Wenzong, and Empress Xiaode.
translations.idiomatic: The second and third western bays would be mu positions, ordering the spirit tablets of Shizu with two empresses, Shizong with two, Renzong with two, Wenzong, and Empress Xiaode.

sentences.zh: 將來穆宗、孝哲後升祔，位居宣宗次。」

translations.literal: When Muzong and Empress Xiaozhe are later elevated for enshrinement, their places will rank next after Xuanzong."
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong and Empress Xiaozhe are later elevated for enshrinement, their places will rank next after Xuanzong."

sentences.zh: 議上，醇親王奕枻韙之，奏言：「寓尊崇於變通，較諸說為當。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Prince Chun Yixuan endorsed it, memorializing: "Embodying reverence within adaptation—this is more fitting than the other proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Prince Chun Yixuan endorsed it, memorializing: "Embodying reverence within adaptation is more fitting than the other proposals.

sentences.zh: 第廟楹有限，國統無窮，增修尚非至計。

translations.literal: Only the temple bays are limited while the imperial line is endless—enlargement and repair are still not the ultimate plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet temple bays are limited while the imperial line is endless—enlargement and repair are still not the ultimate solution.

sentences.zh: 祧廟為歷朝經制，無可避忌。

translations.literal: The distant-ancestor temple is the enduring institution of successive dynasties and cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The distant-ancestor temple is the enduring institution of successive dynasties and cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 請敕自今以往，毋援百世不祧之文，當循親盡則祧之禮，庶鉅典與天地常存。」

translations.literal: We request an edict that from now on one should not invoke the language of never removing for a hundred generations, but should follow the rite of removal when kinship is exhausted, so that the great ritual may endure with Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: We request an edict that from now on one should not invoke the language of never removing for a hundred generations, but should follow the rite of removal when kinship is exhausted, so that the great ritual may endure with Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 於時徐樹銘力主宣宗遺諭，以漢、唐增室為非，今用奉先殿增龕成案，億萬年後，勢難再加。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Shuming strongly upheld Xuanzong's testamentary instruction, holding that Han and Tang enlargement of chambers was wrong; now using the established precedent of adding niches at the Fengxian Hall, after ten thousand years it would be difficult to add again.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Shuming strongly upheld Xuanzong's testamentary instruction, holding that Han and Tang enlargement of chambers was mistaken; using the established precedent of adding niches at the Fengxian Hall, after ten thousand years it would be difficult to add again.

sentences.zh: 宜遵祖訓，豫定昭穆。

translations.literal: One should follow ancestral instruction and fix zhao and mu in advance.
translations.idiomatic: One should follow ancestral instruction and fix zhao and mu in advance.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士鍾佩賢亦以為言，鴻臚寺少卿文碩且請建穆宗寢廟，而文治、寶廷尤力爭並龕簡陋，非永制。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat Academician Zhong Peixian also spoke thus; Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Wen Shuo even requested building Muzong's sleeping temple, while Wen Zhi and Bao Ting especially contended that combining niches was crude and not a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat Academician Zhong Peixian agreed; Vice Director Wen Shuo even requested building Muzong's sleeping temple, while Wen Zhi and Bao Ting especially argued that combining niches was crude and not a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 兩宮太后不獲已，再下王大臣議，兼詢直隸總督李鴻章。

translations.literal: The two Empresses Dowager, unable to do otherwise, again ordered princes and grand ministers to deliberate, and also consulted Zhili Governor-General Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The two Empresses Dowager, unable to resolve the matter, again ordered princes and senior ministers to deliberate and also consulted Zhili Governor-General Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 鴻章言：「周官，匠人營國，世室、明堂，皆止五室。

translations.literal: Hongzhang said: "In the Offices of Zhou, the Master Builder plans the capital; lineage chambers and the Bright Hall each have only five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang argued: "In the Offices of Zhou, the Master Builder plans the capital; lineage chambers and the Bright Hall each have only five chambers.

sentences.zh: 鄭注，五室並在一堂。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary states that the five chambers are all within one hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary states that the five chambers are all within one hall.

sentences.zh: 據此，則硃子所圖世室、親廟以次而南，未盡合制。

translations.literal: According to this, the Zhu Xi school's diagram of lineage chambers and temples for close kin extending southward in sequence does not fully conform to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis, the Zhu Xi school's diagram of lineage chambers and temples for close kin extending southward in sequence does not fully conform to the regulations.

sentences.zh: 至建寢殿、增方殿，古制所無，禮親王等所言，未為無見。

translations.literal: As for building sleeping halls and enlarging square halls, these are not in ancient regulations; what Prince Li and others said was not without insight.
translations.idiomatic: As for building sleeping halls and enlarging square halls, these are not in ancient regulations; Prince Li and others were not without insight.

sentences.zh: 我朝廟制，祖宗神靈，協會一室，一旦遷改，神明奚安？

translations.literal: Our dynasty's temple system gathers the spirits of ancestors and forebears in one chamber; if it were suddenly altered, how would the spirits rest in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's temple system gathers the spirits of ancestors and forebears in one chamber; if it were suddenly altered, how would the spirits rest in peace?

sentences.zh: 太廟重垣，庭墀殿陛，各有恆式。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple's layered walls, courtyard pavements, and hall steps each have fixed forms.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple's layered walls, courtyard pavements, and hall steps each have fixed forms.

sentences.zh: 准古酌今，改廟非便。

translations.literal: Weighing antiquity and considering the present, altering the temple is not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing antiquity against the present, altering the temple is not expedient.

sentences.zh: 因時立制，自以援奉先殿增龕例為宜。

translations.literal: Establishing institutions according to the times, it is fitting to invoke the precedent of adding niches at the Fengxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing institutions according to the times, it is fitting to invoke the precedent of adding niches at the Fengxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 議者或嫌簡略，准古禮祔廟迭遷，亦止改塗易檐，並不大更舊廟。

translations.literal: Some deliberators found this too simple; yet in ancient ritual, when enshrining and shifting in the temple, one only repainted and replaced eaves, without greatly altering the old temple.
translations.idiomatic: Some found this too simple; yet in ancient ritual, enshrinement and shifting involved only repainting and replacing eaves, without greatly altering the old temple.

sentences.zh: 今之龕座，猶晉、宋時坎室，晉華垣建議廟堂以容主為限，無拘常數。

translations.literal: Present niche seats resemble the pit chambers of Jin and Song; Hua Yuan of Jin proposed that temple halls be limited only by capacity for tablets, without binding to a fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Present niche seats resemble the pit chambers of Jin and Song; Hua Yuan of Jin proposed that temple halls be limited only by capacity for tablets, without a fixed number.

sentences.zh: 王導、溫嶠往復商榷，始增坎室。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and Wen Jiao debated back and forth before pit chambers were first increased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Wen Jiao debated back and forth before pit chambers were first increased.

sentences.zh: 宋增八室，蔡襄為圖。

translations.literal: Song added eight chambers; Cai Xiang drew the diagram.
translations.idiomatic: The Song added eight chambers; Cai Xiang drew the diagram.

sentences.zh: 今之增龕，何以異是？」

translations.literal: How does adding niches today differ from this?"
translations.idiomatic: How does adding niches today differ from this?"

sentences.zh: 又謂：「奉先殿即古原廟，與太廟殊。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Fengxian Hall is the ancient separate temple and differs from the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "The Fengxian Hall is the ancient separate temple and differs from the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 然雍正時奏定奉先殿神牌與太廟■A2若畫一。

translations.literal: Yet in the Yongzheng period it was decreed that Fengxian Hall spirit tablets and those of the Imperial Ancestral Temple [text damaged in source] were as if drawn with one compass.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Yongzheng period it was decreed that Fengxian Hall spirit tablets and those of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were wholly uniform, as if drawn to one standard.

sentences.zh: 成憲可循，不得謂增龕之制獨不可仿行太廟也。

translations.literal: Established statutes may be followed; one cannot say that the institution of adding niches cannot alone be applied to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Established statutes may be followed; one cannot say that the institution of adding niches cannot be applied to the Imperial Ancestral Temple as well.

sentences.zh: 至祧遷雖常典，而藏主之室，禮無明文。

translations.literal: As for distant removal, though it is the regular statute, the chamber for storing tablets has no explicit text in the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: As for distant removal, though it is the regular statute, the chamber for storing tablets has no explicit text in the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成言周祧主藏於太廟及文武世室，是已祧之主與不遷之祖同處一廟，故廟亦名祧。

translations.literal: Zheng Kangcheng said that Zhou removed tablets were stored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Wen and Wu lineage chambers—thus removed tablets and ancestors never removed dwelt in one temple; hence the temple was also called the distant-ancestor temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Kangcheng said that removed Zhou tablets were stored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Wen and Wu lineage chambers—thus removed tablets and ancestors never removed shared one temple; hence the temple was also called the distant-ancestor temple.

sentences.zh: 晉藏西儲夾室，當時疑其非禮，後世緣為故事。

translations.literal: Jin stored them in the western reserve side chambers; at the time this was doubted as unritual, but later ages took it as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin stored them in the western reserve side chambers; at the time this was doubted as unritual, but later ages took it as precedent.

sentences.zh: 儒家謂古祧夾室，殆為肊辭。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars say the ancient distant-ancestor side chambers were perhaps speculative language.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars say the ancient distant-ancestor side chambers were perhaps speculative language.

sentences.zh: 廟既與古不同，祧亦未容輕議。

translations.literal: Since the temple already differs from antiquity, distant removal also cannot be lightly debated.
translations.idiomatic: Since the temple already differs from antiquity, distant removal also cannot be lightly debated.

sentences.zh: 唯醇親王所陳，為能導皇上以大讓，酌廟制以從宜。」

translations.literal: Only what Prince Chun presented could guide the Emperor in great yielding and adapt the temple system to expediency."
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Chun's proposal could guide the Emperor in great yielding and adapt the temple system to expediency."

sentences.zh: 自此議遂定。

translations.literal: From this the deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: From this the deliberation was settled.

sentences.zh: 五年，穆宗暨孝哲後祔廟，位東序，西鄉，次宣宗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Muzong together with Empress Xiaozhe were enshrined in the temple, their places in the eastern row facing west, next after Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Muzong together with Empress Xiaozhe were installed in the temple in the eastern row facing west, next after Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 七年，孝貞後升祔，次孝德。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Empress Xiaozhen was elevated for enshrinement, next after Xiaode.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Empress Xiaozhen was elevated for enshrinement, placed next after Xiaode.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，孝欽後升祔，次孝貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Empress Xiaoqin was elevated for enshrinement, next after Xiaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1, Empress Xiaoqin was elevated for enshrinement, placed next after Xiaozhen.

sentences.zh: 是歲考議德宗祔廟事，禮臣言：「兄弟同昭穆，但主穆位空一室。」

translations.literal: That year, when deliberating Dezong's enshrinement in the temple, the ritual officials said: "Brothers share the same zhao and mu, but the mu position lacks one chamber."
translations.idiomatic: That year, when deliberating Dezong's temple installation, the ritual officials stated: "Brothers share the same zhao and mu, but the mu side lacks one chamber."

sentences.zh: 其餘議禮諸臣，重宗統者，以為異昭穆不便；

translations.literal: Other ministers deliberating on ritual, who emphasized the patriline, held that differing zhao and mu would be inconvenient;
translations.idiomatic: Other ministers deliberating on ritual, who emphasized the patriline, held that differing zhao and mu would be inconvenient;

sentences.zh: 重皇統者，復以為同昭穆不合。

translations.literal: those who emphasized the imperial line again held that sharing zhao and mu was not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: those who emphasized the imperial line again held that sharing zhao and mu was not fitting.

sentences.zh: 而大學士張之洞獨主：「古有祧遷之禮，則兄弟昭穆宜同。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Zhidong alone upheld: "When antiquity had the rite of distant removal, brothers' zhao and mu should be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Zhidong alone argued: "When antiquity had the rite of distant removal, brothers' zhao and mu should be the same.

sentences.zh: 今無祧遷之禮，則兄弟昭穆可異。」

translations.literal: Now that there is no rite of distant removal, brothers' zhao and mu may differ."
translations.idiomatic: Now that there is no rite of distant removal, brothers' zhao and mu may differ."

sentences.zh: 議乃定。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was then settled.

sentences.zh: 其秋，詔曰：「我朝廟制，前殿自太祖以下七世皆南鄉，宣宗以下三世分東西鄉，與古所謂穆北鄉、昭南鄉不同。

translations.literal: That autumn, an edict said: "Our dynasty's temple system: in the front hall, from Taizu down through seven generations all face south; from Xuanzong down, three generations are divided east and west—this differs from antiquity's saying that mu faces north and zhao faces south.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, an edict stated: "Our dynasty's temple system: in the front hall, from Taizu through seven generations all face south; from Xuanzong onward, three generations are divided east and west—this differs from antiquity's rule that mu faces north and zhao faces south.

sentences.zh: 穆、德二廟，同為百世不祧，宜守硃子之說，以昭穆分左右，不以昭穆為尊卑。

translations.literal: The Mu and De temples alike are never removed for a hundred generations; one should uphold the Zhu Xi school's teaching to place left and right by zhao and mu, not to treat zhao and mu as superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The Mu and De temples alike are never removed for a hundred generations; one should uphold the Zhu Xi school's teaching to place left and right by zhao and mu, not to treat zhao and mu as marks of rank.

sentences.zh: 禮緣義起，毋因經說異同，過事拘執。

translations.literal: Ritual arises from meaning; do not, because classical interpretations differ, be overly rigid in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual arises from meaning; do not, because classical interpretations differ, be overly rigid in practice.

sentences.zh: 德宗祔廟，中殿奉西又次楹又五室穆位，前殿位次西旁文宗坐西鄉東穆位。

translations.literal: For Dezong's enshrinement in the temple: in the middle hall, worship on the western third bay and fifth mu chamber; in the front hall, his place next on the west side—Wenzong sits facing west in the eastern mu position.
translations.idiomatic: For Dezong's temple installation: in the middle hall, the western third bay and fifth mu chamber; in the front hall, his place on the west side—Wenzong sits facing west in the eastern mu position.

sentences.zh: 體先朝兼祧之旨，慰列聖在天之靈，垂為定制。

translations.literal: Embodying the former court's intent of dual succession, comforting the spirits of successive sages in Heaven, this is established as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Embodying the former court's intent of dual succession, comforting the spirits of successive sages in Heaven, this is established as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 奉先殿位序亦如之。」

translations.literal: The order of places at the Fengxian Hall is likewise."
translations.idiomatic: The order of places at the Fengxian Hall follows the same arrangement."

sentences.zh: 時饗太宗建國初，遇清明、除夕，躬謁太祖陵，即時饗所由始。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings: at the beginning of Taizong's founding of the state, on Qingming and New Year's Eve he personally visited Taizu's tomb—seasonal offerings originated from this.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings: at the beginning of Taizong's founding of the state, on Qingming and New Year's Eve he personally visited Taizu's tomb—seasonal offerings originated from this practice.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，建太廟成，凡四孟時饗，每月薦新，聖誕、忌辰、清明、中元、歲暮俱致祭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, seasonal offerings were held in all four seasons; monthly offerings of new produce; imperial birthdays, death anniversaries, Qingming, Zhongyuan, and year-end all received sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1, when the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, seasonal offerings were held in all four seasons, with monthly offerings of new produce; imperial birthdays, death anniversaries, Qingming, Zhongyuan, and year-end all received sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 五月獻櫻桃，命薦太廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month cherries were presented and ordered offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month cherries were presented and ordered offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 凡新進果穀，皆先薦乃進御，著為令。

translations.literal: Whenever new fruits and grains arrived, all were first offered before being presented to the Emperor—this was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever new fruits and grains arrived, they were first offered before being presented to the Emperor—this was established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，定時饗制，孟春擇上旬日，三孟用朔日，樂章六奏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the seasonal offering system was fixed: in early spring a day in the first ten-day period was chosen; the three seasonal offerings used the first day of the month; six musical movements were performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, the seasonal offering system was fixed: in early spring a day in the first ten-day period was chosen; the three seasonal offerings used the first day of the month; six musical movements were performed.

sentences.zh: 二年，命祭太廟如奉先殿儀，讀祝、致祭。

translations.literal: In the second year, it was ordered that sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple follow the Fengxian Hall rites, reading the prayer and performing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, it was ordered that sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple follow the Fengxian Hall rites, with prayer reading and full sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 遣官祭福陵、昭陵、四祖廟，止上香燭、供酒果，不讀祝。

translations.literal: Officials were dispatched to sacrifice at the Fuling, Zhaoling, and Temple of the Four Ancestors, offering only incense, candles, wine, and fruit, without reading prayers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to sacrifice at Fuling, Zhaoling, and the Temple of the Four Ancestors, offering only incense, candles, wine, and fruit, without reading prayers.

sentences.zh: 七月朔，秋祭太廟、四祖廟，中元祭陵，並用牛、羊。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, autumn sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Temple of the Four Ancestors, and Zhongyuan sacrifice at the tombs, all used oxen and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month, autumn sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Temple of the Four Ancestors, and Zhongyuan sacrifice at the tombs, all used oxen and sheep.

sentences.zh: 尋定四祖廟祭例視京師，牲用生。

translations.literal: Soon the sacrifice regulations for the Temple of the Four Ancestors were fixed to match the capital, with victims used live.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the sacrifice regulations for the Temple of the Four Ancestors were fixed to match the capital, with live victims.

sentences.zh: 又饗太廟用熟牛，罷晉胙。

translations.literal: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple feast, cooked beef was used and the Jin-style presentation of flesh was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple feast, cooked beef was used and the Jin-style presentation of flesh was abolished.

sentences.zh: 八年，定親饗制，飲福、受胙如圜丘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the personal feast system was fixed; drinking blessing wine and receiving sacrificial flesh followed the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the personal feast system was fixed; drinking blessing wine and receiving sacrificial flesh followed the Circular Mound rites.

sentences.zh: 奏樂備文、武佾舞。

translations.literal: Music was performed with civil and military line dances.
translations.idiomatic: Music was performed with civil and military line dances.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，從禮臣言，祭太廟，質明將事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, following the ritual officials' memorial, sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple began at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12, following the ritual officials' memorial, sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple began at dawn.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，親饗畢，諭曰：「往見贊禮郎宣祝，至朕名，聲不揚。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, when the personal feast was completed, he instructed: "Formerly I observed the ritual officer proclaim the prayer; when it reached my name, his voice was not raised.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, when the personal feast was completed, he instructed: "Formerly I observed the ritual officer proclaim the prayer; when it reached my name, his voice was not raised.

sentences.zh: 禮稱父前子名，子孫通名祖父，豈可慢易？

translations.literal: Ritual says that before the father the son's name is spoken; descendants may use the grandfather's name freely—how can one be disrespectful?
translations.idiomatic: Ritual says that before the father the son's name is spoken; descendants may use the grandfather's name freely—how can one be disrespectful?

sentences.zh: 嗣後垂為戒。」

translations.literal: Hereafter let this stand as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter let this stand as a warning."

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，世宗以廟饗無上香，奠帛、爵無跪獻，命大學士禮臣議增。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, Shizong, because temple feasts had no incense offering and no kneeling presentation of silks and goblets, ordered grand secretaries and ritual officials to deliberate on additions.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 11, Shizong, because temple feasts had no incense offering and no kneeling presentation of silks and goblets, ordered grand secretaries and ritual officials to deliberate on additions.

sentences.zh: 尋議言：「大祀莫重郊壇，孝享莫大配天。

translations.literal: Soon they deliberated and said: "Among great sacrifices none outweighs the suburban altar; among filial feasts none is greater than matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they argued: "Among great sacrifices none outweighs the suburban altar; among filial feasts none is greater than matching Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宗廟典禮，宜視社稷。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple's canonical rites should be regarded like those of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple's canonical rites should be regarded like those of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 祭社稷日，皇帝親詣上香，太廟自宜一例。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain, the Emperor personally goes to offer incense; the Imperial Ancestral Temple should naturally follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain, the Emperor personally offers incense; the Imperial Ancestral Temple should naturally follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 至帛、爵俱不親獻，皇帝立拜位前，所以亞郊壇也。

translations.literal: As for silks and goblets, neither is personally presented; the Emperor stands before the kneeling position—this is to rank it below the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: As for silks and goblets, neither is personally presented; the Emperor stands before the kneeling position—this ranks the rite below the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 仍舊儀便。」

translations.literal: The former rites may remain as they are."
translations.idiomatic: The former rites may remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 又定太廟神牌如奉先殿制，供奉居中。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that Imperial Ancestral Temple spirit tablets follow the Fengxian Hall model, worshipped in the center.
translations.idiomatic: It was further fixed that Imperial Ancestral Temple spirit tablets follow the Fengxian Hall model, enshrined in the center.

sentences.zh: 請牌用太常官，獻帛、爵用侍衛，尋改用宗室官。

translations.literal: Requesting tablets used Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials; presenting silks and goblets used guards—soon changed to use imperial clansmen officials.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting tablets used Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials; presenting silks and goblets used guards—soon changed to imperial clansmen officials.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，定三年持服內，饗廟御禮服作樂如故，唯齋戒用素服，冠綴纓。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, it was fixed that within the three-year mourning period, temple feasts used imperial ceremonial dress and music as before; only for abstention plain dress was used, with cap tassels and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, it was fixed that within the three-year mourning period, temple feasts used imperial ceremonial dress and music as before; only for abstention plain dress was used, with cap tassels and ribbons.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，用禮臣言，祝版書列聖尊諡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, following the ritual officials' memorial, the prayer board recorded successive emperors' honorific posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2, following the ritual officials' memorial, the prayer board recorded successive emperors' honorific posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 香帛送燎時行中路，帝轉立東旁，俟奉祝帛官出，復位，如祀郊壇式。

translations.literal: When incense and silks were sent to the brazier along the central path, the Emperor turned to stand on the east side, waiting until the officer bearing prayer silks emerged, then returned to position—as at suburban altar sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When incense and silks were sent to the brazier along the central path, the Emperor turned to stand on the east side, waiting until the officer bearing prayer silks emerged, then returned to position—as at suburban altar sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尋定每日上香，守廟官行禮。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that incense was offered daily, with temple-guarding officials performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was fixed that incense was offered daily, performed by temple-guarding officials.

sentences.zh: 朔望用太常官。

translations.literal: On new-moon and full-moon days, Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials were used.
translations.idiomatic: On new-moon and full-moon days, Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 嗣改宗室王公番行。

translations.literal: Subsequently it was changed to imperial clansmen princes serving in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently imperial clansmen princes were assigned to serve in rotation.

sentences.zh: 十二年，諭太廟獻帛、爵用宗室官，俾習禮儀、鎔氣質。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict ordered that at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, presenting silks and goblets use imperial clansmen officials, so they might practice ritual propriety and refine their character.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, an edict ordered that at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, presenting silks and goblets be entrusted to imperial clansmen officials, so they might practice ritual propriety and refine their character.

sentences.zh: 敕宗人府王公監視，後復定後殿獻帛、爵用覺羅官。

translations.literal: Princes of the Imperial Clan Court were ordered to supervise; later it was again fixed that in the rear hall, presenting silks and goblets use Aisin Gioro officials.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the Imperial Clan Court were ordered to supervise; later it was again fixed that in the rear hall, presenting silks and goblets be entrusted to Aisin Gioro officials.

sentences.zh: 向例，饗廟，帝乘輿出宮，至太和門外改乘輦。

translations.literal: By former practice, at temple feasts, the Emperor rode in the imperial carriage out of the palace; outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony he changed to the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: By former practice, at temple feasts the Emperor rode in the imperial carriage out of the palace and, outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, changed to the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 入街門，至神路右，步入南門，詣戟門幄次。

translations.literal: Entering the street gate, reaching the right of the spirit path, walking in through the south gate, proceeding to the curtained pavilion at the Halberd Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the street gate, reached the right side of the spirit path, walked in through the south gate, and proceeded to the curtained pavilion at the Halberd Gate.

sentences.zh: 入升東階，進前殿門，就拜位。

translations.literal: Entering, ascending the east steps, proceeding through the front hall gate, taking up the kneeling position.
translations.idiomatic: He entered, ascended the east steps, passed through the front hall gate, and took up the kneeling position.

sentences.zh: 禮成，出如初。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he exited as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he exited by the same route.

sentences.zh: 凡入門皆左。

translations.literal: In all cases of entering gates, one kept to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In every case of entering a gate, one kept to the left.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，帝年漸高，略減儀節。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, as the Emperor's age grew advanced, ceremonial details were somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, as the Emperor's age advanced, ceremonial details were somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 入廟時，改自闕左門輦入西北門，至廟北門外，輿入。

translations.literal: When entering the temple, the route was changed: from the Left Gate of the Gate Tower one entered by palanquin through the northwest gate, to outside the temple's north gate, then entered by carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When entering the temple, the route was changed: from the Left Gate of the Gate Tower he entered by palanquin through the northwest gate, reached the outside of the temple's north gate, and then entered by carriage.

sentences.zh: 至戟門外東階下。

translations.literal: He reached below the east steps outside the Halberd Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the foot of the east steps outside the Halberd Gate.

sentences.zh: 步入門，升階進殿。

translations.literal: Walking in through the gate, ascending the steps and entering the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He walked in through the gate, ascended the steps, and entered the hall.

sentences.zh: 行禮畢，出亦如之。

translations.literal: When the rite was performed and complete, exiting likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he exited in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，定時饗前殿座次。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, seating order for seasonal offerings in the front hall was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, seating order for seasonal offerings in the front hall was fixed.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗、世祖皇考、妣皆南鄉，聖祖皇考、妣東位西鄉，世宗皇考、妣西位東鄉，高宗皇考、妣東次西鄉。

translations.literal: Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu's imperial father and mother all faced south; Shengzu's imperial father and mother occupied the eastern seat facing west; Shizong's imperial father and mother occupied the western seat facing east; Gaozong's imperial father and mother occupied the eastern secondary seat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu's imperial father and mother all faced south; Shengzu's imperial father and mother sat in the eastern seat facing west; Shizong's imperial father and mother sat in the western seat facing east; Gaozong's imperial father and mother sat in the eastern secondary seat facing west.

sentences.zh: 以後帝、後位次仿此。

translations.literal: For later emperors and empresses, seating order followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: For later emperors and empresses, seating order followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 八年孟春時饗，禮臣卜吉初六日，仁宗以前三日致齋。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for the first-month seasonal offering, ritual officials divined an auspicious day on the sixth; Renzong observed abstention three days prior.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, for the first-month seasonal offering, ritual officials chose the sixth as the auspicious day; Renzong observed abstention three days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 會逢高宗忌辰，服色未協，命改初八日。

translations.literal: It happened to coincide with Gaozong's death anniversary; mourning attire was incompatible, so the order was changed to the eighth day.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to coincide with Gaozong's death anniversary, and mourning attire was incompatible, so the rite was moved to the eighth.

sentences.zh: 嗣是春饗皆擇正月初八、九、十等日行之。

translations.literal: Thereafter spring seasonal offerings were all held on the eighth, ninth, tenth, and similar days of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter spring seasonal offerings were held on the eighth, ninth, tenth, or similar days of the first month.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，諭廟饗謝福胙如祀社稷儀，王公百官隨行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, an edict ordered that at temple feasts, thanksgiving for blessings and distribution of sacrificial meat follow the rites for sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain; princes and officials all performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4, an edict ordered that at temple feasts, thanksgiving for blessings and distribution of sacrificial meat follow the rites for sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain, with princes and officials performing the three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 穆宗、德宗初立，時饗、祫祭遣親王代，逮親政始躬蒞。

translations.literal: When Muzong and Dezong first ascended, seasonal offerings and collective ancestral sacrifice were delegated to princes; only when they personally assumed government did they attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong and Dezong first ascended, seasonal offerings and collective ancestral sacrifice were delegated to princes; only after they personally assumed government did they attend in person.

sentences.zh: 宣統朝攝政王攝行。

translations.literal: In the Xuantong reign, the regent performed the rites on behalf of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuantong reign, the regent performed the rites in the Emperor's stead.

sentences.zh: 祫祭歷代禘、祫分祭，禮說繽紛，罔衷古訓。

translations.literal: Through the ages of collective ancestral sacrifice, di and xia were performed as separate sacrifices; ritual interpretations were numerous and conflicting, with no agreement on ancient teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Through the ages, collective ancestral sacrifice involved di and xia as separate rites; ritual interpretations were numerous and conflicting, with no agreement on ancient teachings.

sentences.zh: 清制有祫無禘。

translations.literal: The Qing system had xia but not di.
