translations.idiomatic: The Qing system observed collective ancestral sacrifice (xiá) but not di.

sentences.zh: 除夕饗廟，實始太宗，世祖本之，著為祭典。

translations.literal: Year-end-eve temple feasts actually began with Taizong; Shizu followed his example, and it was established as sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end-eve temple feasts actually began with Taizong; Shizu followed his example, and the practice was established as sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，左副都御史袁懋功請舉祫祭，以彰孝治。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Maogong requested collective ancestral sacrifice to manifest filial governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Maogong requested collective ancestral sacrifice to manifest filial governance.

sentences.zh: 乃定歲除前一日大祫，移後殿、中殿神主奉前殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was fixed that on the day before New Year's Eve the great xia would be held, moving spirit tablets from the rear and middle halls to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was fixed that on the day before New Year's Eve the great collective ancestral sacrifice would be held, with spirit tablets moved from the rear and middle halls to the front hall.

sentences.zh: 四祖、太祖南鄉，太宗東位西鄉。

translations.literal: The Four Ancestors and Taizu faced south; Taizong occupied the eastern seat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Ancestors and Taizu faced south; Taizong sat in the eastern seat facing west.

sentences.zh: 先一日遣官告後殿、中殿，致齋視牲。

translations.literal: On the day before, officials were dispatched to announce at the rear and middle halls; abstention was observed and sacrificial animals inspected.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, officials were dispatched to announce at the rear and middle halls; abstention was observed and the sacrificial animals inspected.

sentences.zh: 屆日世祖親詣，禮如時饗，自是歲以為常。

translations.literal: On the appointed day Shizu attended in person; the rite was as for seasonal offerings; thereafter it became annual practice.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Shizu attended in person; the rite followed seasonal offerings; thereafter it became annual practice.

sentences.zh: 尋定祫祭樂舞陳殿外。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that music and dance for collective ancestral sacrifice be arrayed outside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was fixed that music and dance for collective ancestral sacrifice be stationed outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，御史李時謙請行禘祭。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period, Censor Li Shiqian requested performance of di sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi period, Censor Li Shiqian requested that di sacrifice be performed.

sentences.zh: 禮臣張玉書上言：「考禮制言禘不一，有謂虞、夏禘黃帝，殷、周禘嚳，皆配祭圜丘者；

translations.literal: Ritual Minister Zhang Yushu memorialized: "Examining ritual systems, accounts of di differ: some say that in Yu and Xia, Huangdi was honored in di, and in Yin and Zhou, Ku—all as mates at the Circular Mound;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Minister Zhang Yushu argued: "Examining ritual systems, accounts of di differ: some say that in Yu and Xia, Huangdi was honored in di, and in Yin and Zhou, Ku—all as mates at the Circular Mound;

sentences.zh: 有謂祖所自出為感生帝，而祭之南郊者；

translations.literal: some say the emperor from whom the ancestor descended was the birth-responding emperor, sacrificed at the southern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: some say the emperor from whom the ancestor descended was the birth-responding emperor, sacrificed at the southern suburb;

sentences.zh: 有謂圜丘、方澤、宗廟為三禘者：先儒皆辯其非。

translations.literal: some say the Circular Mound, Square Pond, and Ancestral Temple are the three di—the former Confucians all argued against this.
translations.idiomatic: some say the Circular Mound, Square Pond, and Ancestral Temple are the three di—the former Confucians all rejected this.

sentences.zh: 而宗廟之禘，說尤不一。

translations.literal: Yet regarding di in the ancestral temple, interpretations are especially varied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet regarding di in the ancestral temple, interpretations are especially varied.

sentences.zh: 或謂禘止及毀廟，或謂長發詩為殷禘，雍詩為周禘，而親廟、毀廟兼祭者。

translations.literal: Some say di reaches only destroyed temples; some say the Changfa ode is Yin's di, the Yong ode Zhou's di, sacrificing both close temples and destroyed temples.
translations.idiomatic: Some say di reaches only destroyed temples; some say the Changfa ode describes Yin's di and the Yong ode Zhou's di, sacrificing both close temples and destroyed temples together.

sentences.zh: 唯唐趙匡、陸淳以為禘異於祫，不兼群廟。

translations.literal: Only Tang's Zhao Kuang and Lu Chun held that di differs from xia and does not join all temples.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao Kuang and Lu Chun of Tang held that di differs from xia and does not join all temples.

sentences.zh: 王者立始祖廟，推祖所自出之帝，以始祖配之，故名禘。

translations.literal: When a king establishes the temple of the founding ancestor, he extends honor to the emperor from whom the ancestor descended, with the founding ancestor as mate—hence the name di.
translations.idiomatic: When a king establishes the temple of the founding ancestor, he extends honor to the emperor from whom the ancestor descended, with the founding ancestor as mate—hence the name di.

sentences.zh: 至三年一祫，五年一禘，說始漢儒，後人宗之。

translations.literal: As for xia every three years and di every five years, this teaching began with Han Confucians; later generations followed it.
translations.idiomatic: As for xia every three years and di every five years, this teaching began with Han Confucians, and later generations followed it.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐、宋禘禮，並未考始祖所自出，止五歲中合群廟之祖，行祫禘於宗廟而已。

translations.literal: Han, Tang, and Song di rites never investigated the founding ancestor's descent; they only united ancestors of all temples within five years, performing xia and di in the ancestral temple—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Tang, and Song di rites never investigated the founding ancestor's descent; they only united ancestors of all temples within five years, performing xia and di in the ancestral temple—that was all.

sentences.zh: 大抵夏、商以前有禘祭，而厥制莫詳。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, before Xia and Shang there was di sacrifice, but its institution is not detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Generally speaking, before Xia and Shang there was di sacrifice, but its institution is not known in detail.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐以後有禘名，而與祫無別。

translations.literal: After Han and Tang there was the name di, but it differed not from xia.
translations.idiomatic: After Han and Tang there was the name di, but it differed not from xia.

sentences.zh: 周以后稷為始祖，以帝嚳為所自出，而太廟中無嚳位，故祫祭不及。

translations.literal: Zhou took Houji as founding ancestor and Di Ku as the descent line; yet in the Great Temple there was no place for Ku, so collective ancestral sacrifice did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou took Houji as founding ancestor and Di Ku as the descent line; yet in the Great Temple there was no place for Ku, so collective ancestral sacrifice did not reach him.

sentences.zh: 至禘祭乃設嚳位，以稷配焉。

translations.literal: Only at di sacrifice was Ku's place set, with Houji as mate.
translations.idiomatic: Only at di sacrifice was Ku's place set, with Houji as mate.

sentences.zh: 行於後代，不能盡合。

translations.literal: Applied in later ages, it could not fully accord.
translations.idiomatic: Applied in later ages, it could not fully accord with the ancient model.

sentences.zh: 故宋神宗罷禘禮。

translations.literal: Hence Emperor Shenzong of Song abolished di rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Emperor Shenzong of Song abolished di rites.

sentences.zh: 明洪武初或請舉行，眾議不果。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu of Ming, some requested its performance; deliberation did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu of Ming, some requested its performance, but deliberation did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，乃立虛位，祀皇初祖帝，以太祖配，事涉不經，禮亦旋罷。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era, they established an empty seat, sacrificing the Primal Ancestor Emperor with Taizu as mate—the matter involved impropriety, and the rite was soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era, they established an empty seat, sacrificing the Primal Ancestor Emperor with Taizu as mate—the matter was irregular, and the rite was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 國家初定鼎，追上四祖尊稱，立廟崇祀，自肇祖始。

translations.literal: When our state first established rule, it conferred honorific titles on the Four Ancestors, built temples for exalted worship, beginning from the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When our state first established rule, it conferred honorific titles on the Four Ancestors, built temples for exalted worship, beginning from the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖功德隆盛，當為萬世廟祖，而推所自出，則締造大業，肇祖最著。

translations.literal: Taizu's merit was grand and abundant; he should be the temple ancestor for ten thousand generations; yet tracing descent, the Founding Ancestor who established the great enterprise was most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's merit was grand and abundant; he should be the temple ancestor for ten thousand generations; yet tracing descent, the Founding Ancestor who established the great enterprise was most prominent.

sentences.zh: 今太廟祭禮，四孟分祭前、後殿，以各伸其尊。

translations.literal: Present Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices: in the four first months, separate sacrifices in front and rear halls, each extending its honor.
translations.idiomatic: Present Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifices: in the four first months, separate offerings in the front and rear halls, each extending its due honor.

sentences.zh: 歲暮祫饗前殿，以同將其敬。

translations.literal: At year's end, xia feast in the front hall unites their reverence.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end, collective ancestral sacrifice in the front hall unites their reverence.

sentences.zh: 一歲屢申祼獻，仁孝誠敬，已無不極。

translations.literal: Within one year, libation and presentation are repeatedly performed; benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence have already reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year, libation and presentation are repeatedly performed; benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence have already reached the utmost.

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，可不必行。」

translations.literal: Di every five years need not be performed."
translations.idiomatic: Di every five years need not be performed."

sentences.zh: 遂寢其議。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was thereupon set aside.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年大祫，帝親詣肇祖位前上香，餘遣皇子親王分詣，復位行禮如常儀。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, at the great collective ancestral sacrifice, the Emperor personally went to the Founding Ancestor's seat to offer incense; for the remainder he dispatched princes and imperial sons to attend separately, then returned to position and performed the rite as usual.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37, at the great collective ancestral sacrifice, the Emperor personally offered incense before the Founding Ancestor's seat; for the remainder he dispatched princes and imperial sons to attend separately, then returned to position and performed the rite as usual.

sentences.zh: 詣廟節文減之如時饗。

translations.literal: Ceremonial details for approaching the temple were reduced as for seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial details for approaching the temple were reduced, as for seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 六十年將屆歸政，九廟俱親上香。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, as abdication neared, the Emperor personally offered incense at all nine temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, as abdication neared, he personally offered incense at all nine temples.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，定歲暮祫祭，前殿座位視時饗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, year-end collective ancestral sacrifice was fixed; front hall seating followed seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, year-end collective ancestral sacrifice was fixed; front hall seating followed seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，文宗疾甫平，親王代行祫祭，然先祭時猶親詣拜跪焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, Wenzong's illness had just abated; a prince performed collective ancestral sacrifice on his behalf, yet for the prior seasonal offering he still personally went to kneel and prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8, Wenzong's illness had just abated; a prince performed collective ancestral sacrifice on his behalf, yet for the prior seasonal offering he still personally went to kneel and prostrate.

sentences.zh: 其因時祫祭者，古禮天子三年喪畢，合先祖神饗之，謂之吉祭。

translations.literal: As for occasional collective ancestral sacrifice: in ancient rite, when the Son of Heaven's three-year mourning was complete, the spirits of forebears were feasted together—this was called auspicious sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Occasional collective ancestral sacrifice followed ancient rite: when the Son of Heaven's three-year mourning was complete, the spirits of forebears were feasted together—this was called auspicious sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，吏部尚書硃軾言：「皇上至仁大孝，喪三年如一日，今服制竟，請祫祭太廟，即吉釋哀。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, Minister of Personnel Zhu Shi said: "Your Majesty's utmost benevolence and great filial piety have observed mourning for three years as one day; now the mourning period is complete—I request collective ancestral sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, auspiciously releasing grief."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, Minister of Personnel Zhu Shi argued: "Your Majesty's utmost benevolence and great filial piety have observed mourning for three years as one day; now the mourning period is complete—I request collective ancestral sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, auspiciously releasing grief."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Imperial approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，帝詣廟行祫祭，如歲暮大祫儀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the Emperor went to the temple to perform collective ancestral sacrifice, following the rites of the year-end great xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, the Emperor went to the temple to perform collective ancestral sacrifice, following the rites of the year-end great xia.

sentences.zh: 自後服竟行祫祭仿此。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when mourning was complete, collective ancestral sacrifice followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when mourning was complete, collective ancestral sacrifice followed this model.

sentences.zh: 加上諡號崇德元年，太宗受尊號，追封始祖為澤王、高祖慶王、曾祖昌王、祖福王，上太祖武皇帝、孝慈皇后尊諡。

translations.literal: In the first year of adding honorific titles, the Chongde era, Taizong received an honorific title; the Founding Ancestor was retroactively enfeoffed as Prince Ze, the High Ancestor as Prince Qing, the Great-Grandfather as Prince Chang, and the Grandfather as Prince Fu; honorific posthumous titles were conferred on the Martial Emperor Taizu and Empress Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of adding honorific titles, the Chongde era, Taizong received an honorific title; the Founding Ancestor was retroactively enfeoffed as Prince Ze, the High Ancestor as Prince Qing, the Great-Grandfather as Prince Chang, and the Grandfather as Prince Fu; honorific posthumous titles were conferred on the Martial Emperor Taizu and Empress Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 即日躬祀太廟。

translations.literal: That same day he personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 翼日，百官表賀。

translations.literal: The next day, officials presented congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, officials presented congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，進太祖、孝慈後、太宗玉冊、玉寶，奉安太廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, jade books and jade seals for Taizu, Empress Xiaoci, and Taizong were presented and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, jade books and jade seals for Taizu, Empress Xiaoci, and Taizong were presented and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 冊長八寸八分，廣三寸九分，厚四分。

translations.literal: The book was eight cun and eight fen long, three cun and nine fen wide, and four fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The book measured eight cun and eight fen long, three cun and nine fen wide, and four fen thick.

sentences.zh: 冊數十，面底二頁鐫升降龍。

translations.literal: The book had several dozen pages; the front and back covers were carved with ascending and descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The book had several dozen pages; the front and back covers were carved with ascending and descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 寶方四寸二分，厚一寸五分，紐高二寸七分，長四寸二分，廣三寸五分，寶盝金質。

translations.literal: The seal was square, four cun and two fen on a side, one cun and five fen thick; the knob was two cun and seven fen high, four cun and two fen long, and three cun and five fen wide; the seal case was of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was square, four cun and two fen on a side, one cun and five fen thick; the knob was two cun and seven fen high, four cun and two fen long, and three cun and five fen wide; the seal case was of gold.

sentences.zh: 凡太廟冊、寶皆用玉，色青白，冊文用驪體，寶文如諡號，曰「某祖某宗某皇帝之寶」，後曰「某皇后之寶」。

translations.literal: All Imperial Ancestral Temple books and seals used jade of bluish-white color; book inscriptions used li script; seal inscriptions followed the posthumous title, reading "Seal of Such-and-Such Ancestor, Such-and-Such Emperor," and for empresses, "Seal of Such-and-Such Empress."
translations.idiomatic: All Imperial Ancestral Temple books and seals were of bluish-white jade; book inscriptions used li script; seal inscriptions followed the posthumous title, reading "Seal of Such-and-Such Ancestor, Such-and-Such Emperor," and for empresses, "Seal of Such-and-Such Empress."

sentences.zh: 五年，追尊澤王肇祖原皇帝，妣原皇后；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, posthumous elevation was conferred on Prince Ze, the Founding Ancestor, as Emperor Yuan, and his consort as Empress Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, posthumous elevation was conferred on Prince Ze, the Founding Ancestor, as Emperor Yuan, and his consort as Empress Yuan;

sentences.zh: 慶王興祖直皇帝，妣直皇后；

translations.literal: Prince Qing, the High Ancestor, as Emperor Zhi, and his consort as Empress Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qing, the High Ancestor, as Emperor Zhi, and his consort as Empress Zhi;

sentences.zh: 昌王景祖翼皇帝，妣翼皇后；

translations.literal: Prince Chang, the Great-Grandfather Ancestor, as Emperor Yi, and his consort as Empress Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chang, the Great-Grandfather Ancestor, as Emperor Yi, and his consort as Empress Yi;

sentences.zh: 福王顯祖宣皇帝，妣宣皇后。

translations.literal: Prince Fu, the Grandfather Ancestor, as Emperor Xuan, and his consort as Empress Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu, the Grandfather Ancestor, as Emperor Xuan, and his consort as Empress Xuan.

sentences.zh: 奉安訖，致禮如時饗。

translations.literal: When enshrinement was complete, sacrifice was performed as for seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When enshrinement was complete, sacrifice was performed as for seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 越三日，慶賀如儀。

translations.literal: Three days later, congratulatory rites were performed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, congratulatory rites were performed according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 七年，上孝端文皇后尊諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Xiaoduanwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Xiaoduanwen.

sentences.zh: 九年，進四祖帝後冊寶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, books and seals for the Four Ancestors, emperors and empresses, were presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, books and seals for the Four Ancestors, emperors and empresses, were presented.

sentences.zh: 十八年，上世祖尊諡，前期齋戒，遣官祭告天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Shizu's honorific posthumous title was conferred; beforehand abstention was observed, and officials were dispatched to announce and sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Shizu's honorific posthumous title was conferred; beforehand abstention was observed, and officials were dispatched to announce and sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 屆日，帝素服御太和門，閱冊、寶訖，大學士奉安采亭，校尉舁行，導以御杖，駕從之。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, the Emperor in plain dress presided at the Gate of Supreme Harmony; when the books and seals had been reviewed, grand secretaries placed them in the ceremonial pavilion; guards carried them in procession, led by imperial staves, and the imperial retinue followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, the Emperor in plain dress presided at the Gate of Supreme Harmony; when the books and seals had been reviewed, grand secretaries placed them in the ceremonial pavilion; guards carried them in procession, led by imperial staves, with the imperial retinue following.

sentences.zh: 王公百官各於所立位跪俟，隨行。

translations.literal: Princes and officials each knelt waiting at their assigned positions and followed in procession.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and officials each knelt waiting at their assigned positions and followed in procession.

sentences.zh: 至壽皇殿大門外降輦，入左門，采亭入右門。

translations.literal: Reaching outside the great gate of the Hall of Imperial Longevity, he descended from the palanquin; entering the left gate, the ceremonial pavilion entered the right gate.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching outside the great gate of the Hall of Imperial Longevity, he descended from the palanquin; entering the left gate, the ceremonial pavilion entered the right gate.

sentences.zh: 大學士二人跪奉冊寶陳案上，帝就位，率群臣行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: Two grand secretaries knelt and presented the books and seals, placing them on the table; the Emperor took his position and led the ministers in the three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: Two grand secretaries knelt and presented the books and seals, placing them on the table; the Emperor took his position and led the ministers in the three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 贊引奏「跪」，奏「進冊」，奉冊大學士跪左，進帝跪獻。

translations.literal: The usher announced "Kneel," then announced "Present the book"; the grand secretary bearing the book knelt on the left, advanced, and the Emperor knelt to present it.
translations.idiomatic: The usher announced "Kneel," then announced "Present the book"; the grand secretary bearing the book knelt on the left, advanced, and the Emperor knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 畢，授右跪大學士陳中案。

translations.literal: When complete, he handed it to the grand secretary kneeling on the right, who placed it on the central table.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, he handed it to the grand secretary kneeling on the right, who placed it on the central table.

sentences.zh: 奏「進寶」，如初。

translations.literal: The announcement "Present the seal" was made, as before.
translations.idiomatic: The announcement "Present the seal" was made, as before.

sentences.zh: 奏「宣冊」，宣冊官跪宣：「上尊諡曰體天隆運英睿欽文大德弘功至仁純孝章皇帝，廟號世祖。」

translations.literal: The announcement "Proclaim the book" was made; the proclamation officer knelt and proclaimed: "The honorific posthumous title reads: Emperor Zhang, embodying Heaven, elevating fortune, perspicacious and reverent in culture, great in virtue and expansive in merit, utmost in benevolence and pure in filial piety; temple name Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: The announcement "Proclaim the book" was made; the proclamation officer knelt and proclaimed: "The honorific posthumous title reads: Emperor Zhang, embodying Heaven, elevating fortune, perspicacious and reverent in culture, great in virtue and expansive in merit, utmost in benevolence and pure in filial piety; temple name Shizu."

sentences.zh: 宣冊訖，奏「宣寶」，儀亦如之。

translations.literal: When the proclamation of the book was complete, the announcement "Proclaim the seal" was made; the rite likewise followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation of the book was complete, the announcement "Proclaim the seal" was made; the rite proceeded likewise.

sentences.zh: 行禮三跪九叩，致祭同時饗。

translations.literal: The three kneelings and nine kowtows were performed; sacrifice was conducted as for seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The three kneelings and nine kowtows were performed; sacrifice was conducted as for seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 畢，奉絹冊、寶、祝帛如燎所焚之。

translations.literal: When complete, silk books, seals, and prayer silks were taken to the brazier site and burned.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, silk books, seals, and prayer silks were taken to the brazier site and burned.

sentences.zh: 大學士二人，奉香冊、寶導梓宮奉安，一跪三叩，翼日頒詔天下。

translations.literal: Two grand secretaries, bearing incense books and seals, led the imperial coffin to enshrinement; one kneeling and three kowtows were performed; the next day an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Two grand secretaries, bearing incense books and seals, led the imperial coffin to enshrinement; one kneeling and three kowtows were performed; the next day an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡上大行帝後尊諡，香冊、香寶獻几筵後，奉安山陵，絹冊、寶送燎，玉冊、玉寶卜吉藏之太廟，後仿此。

translations.literal: Whenever honorific posthumous titles were conferred on a deceased emperor or empress, after incense books and incense seals were presented at the spirit couch, they were enshrined at the imperial tomb; silk books and seals were sent to the brazier; jade books and jade seals, on an auspicious day chosen by divination, were stored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple—later cases followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever honorific posthumous titles were conferred on a deceased emperor or empress, after incense books and incense seals were presented at the spirit couch, they were enshrined at the imperial tomb; silk books and seals were sent to the brazier; jade books and jade seals, on an auspicious day chosen by divination, were stored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple—later cases followed this model.

sentences.zh: 初太祖尊諡曰承天廣運聖德神功肇紀立極仁孝武皇帝，太宗曰應天興國弘德彰武寬溫仁聖睿孝文皇帝。

translations.literal: Initially Taizu's honorific posthumous title read: Martial Emperor Wu, receiving Heaven, broadly extending fortune, sacred in virtue and miraculous in merit, founding the chronicle and establishing the pole, benevolent and filial; Taizong's read: Literary Emperor Wen, responding to Heaven, raising the state, expanding virtue and displaying martial prowess, broad, mild, benevolent, sage, perspicacious, and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Taizu's honorific posthumous title read: Martial Emperor Wu, receiving Heaven, broadly extending fortune, sacred in virtue and miraculous in merit, founding the chronicle and establishing the pole, benevolent and filial; Taizong's read: Literary Emperor Wen, responding to Heaven, raising the state, expanding virtue and displaying martial prowess, broad, mild, benevolent, sage, perspicacious, and filial.

sentences.zh: 聖祖纘業，加太祖「睿武弘文定業」六字，更廟號高皇帝；

translations.literal: Shengzu continued the enterprise, adding six characters to Taizu—"Perspicacious in Martial Prowess, Expansive in Culture, Stabilizing the Enterprise"—and changing the temple name to High Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Shengzu continued the enterprise, adding six characters to Taizu—"Perspicacious in Martial Prowess, Expansive in Culture, Stabilizing the Enterprise"—and changing the temple name to High Emperor;

sentences.zh: 太宗「隆道顯功」四字，廟號如故。

translations.literal: To Taizong he added four characters—"Elevating the Way, Displaying Merit"—while the temple name remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: To Taizong he added four characters—"Elevating the Way, Displaying Merit"—while the temple name remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 用禮臣言，俟世祖祔饗後行禮。

translations.literal: Following the ritual officials' advice, one waited until after Shizu was enshrined with collateral worship before performing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Following the ritual officials' advice, the rites were deferred until after Shizu was installed in the ancestral temple with collateral worship.

sentences.zh: 明年，上慈和皇太后尊諡。

translations.literal: The following year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Dowager Cihe.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Dowager Cihe.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上孝庄太皇太后尊諡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Grand Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Grand Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，上孝惠皇太后尊諡，後，聖祖嫡母也。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Dowager Xiaohui; the empress was Shengzu's lawful mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year, an honorific posthumous title was conferred on Empress Dowager Xiaohui, Shengzu's lawful mother.

sentences.zh: 祔廟日，命安神位慈和上。

translations.literal: On the day of enshrinement in the temple, an order was issued to place the spirit seat above Cihe.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of installation in the ancestral temple, an order was issued to place her spirit seat above Cihe.

sentences.zh: 六十一年冬，世宗諭廷臣：「皇考繼統，本應稱宗，但經云：祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, winter, Shizong instructed the court ministers: "My imperial father succeeded to the throne and ought by rights to be styled a Manifest Ancestor (zong); yet the classic says: 'An ancestor (zu) has merit; a manifestation (zong) has virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, winter, Shizong instructed the court ministers: "My imperial father succeeded to the throne and ought by rights to be styled a Manifest Ancestor; yet the classic says: 'An ancestor has merit; a manifestation has virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇考手定太平，論繼統為守成，論勛業為開創，宜崇祖號，以副豐功。

translations.literal: My imperial father personally established peace; judged by succession he preserved what was achieved, yet judged by achievement he founded anew—he should be honored with the title of Ancestor, to match his abundant merit.
translations.idiomatic: My imperial father personally established peace; judged by succession he preserved what was achieved, yet judged by achievement he founded anew—he should be honored with the title of Ancestor, to match his abundant merit.

sentences.zh: 其確議之。」

translations.literal: Deliberate this thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate this thoroughly."

sentences.zh: 議言：「按禮經：有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，祖顓頊而宗堯。

translations.literal: The deliberation stated: "According to the Book of Rites: the Youyu clan performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku, honored Zhuanxu as ancestor and Yao as manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation stated: "According to the Book of Rites: the Youyu clan performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku, honored Zhuanxu as ancestor and Yao as manifestation.

sentences.zh: 而舜典云：舜格文祖。

translations.literal: Yet the Canon of Shun says: Shun arrived at the Literary Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Canon of Shun says: Shun arrived at the Literary Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 注曰堯廟。

translations.literal: The commentary says this means Yao's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says this means Yao's temple.

sentences.zh: 歸格藝祖，復釋為堯之祖。

translations.literal: Returning to honor the Founding Ancestor is again explained as Yao's ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to honor the Founding Ancestor is again explained as Yao's ancestor.

sentences.zh: 合之祖顓頊，則有三祖矣。

translations.literal: Combined with honoring Zhuanxu as ancestor, there would then be three ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Combined with honoring Zhuanxu as ancestor, there would then be three ancestors.

sentences.zh: 宋陳祥道云：凡配天者皆得稱祖。

translations.literal: Song Chen Xiangdao said: whoever mates with Heaven may be called ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chen Xiangdao said: whoever mates with Heaven may be called ancestor.

sentences.zh: 國語展禽謂有虞氏祖高陽而郊堯，堯所以稱文祖也。

translations.literal: In the Discourses, Zhan Qin said the Youyu clan honored Gaoyang as ancestor and sacrificed to Yao at the suburb; hence Yao was called the Literary Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Discourses, Zhan Qin said the Youyu clan honored Gaoyang as ancestor and sacrificed to Yao at the suburb; hence Yao was called the Literary Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 顓頊至堯，並黃帝子孫，故皆稱祖。

translations.literal: From Zhuanxu to Yao, all were descendants of the Yellow Emperor; hence all were called ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuanxu to Yao, all were descendants of the Yellow Emperor; hence all were called ancestors.

sentences.zh: 又周禮大宗伯：祫、禘、追享、朝享。

translations.literal: Furthermore, in the Grand Minister of the Zhou Rites: xia, di, retrospective feast, and court feast.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in the Grand Minister of the Zhou Rites: xia, di, retrospective feast, and court feast.

sentences.zh: 解云：古者朝廟合群祖而祭焉，故祫曰朝饗，以合群祖為不足，復禘其所自出，故禘曰追饗。

translations.literal: The commentary says: in antiquity the court temple assembled all ancestors in sacrifice, hence xia is called court feast; deeming assembly of all ancestors insufficient, they additionally performed di to the one from whom descent came, hence di is called retrospective feast.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: in antiquity the court temple assembled all ancestors in sacrifice, hence xia is called court feast; deeming assembly of all ancestors insufficient, they additionally performed di to the one from whom descent came, hence di is called retrospective feast.

sentences.zh: 夫祖所自出，始祖也，其下曰群祖，則自始祖以下皆可稱祖矣。」

translations.literal: The ancestor from whom one descends is the founding ancestor; those below are called the collective ancestors; thus from the founding ancestor downward all may be called ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: The ancestor from whom one descends is the founding ancestor; those below are called the collective ancestors; thus from the founding ancestor downward all may be called ancestors."

sentences.zh: 又諡議：「帝王功業隆盛，得援祖有功古義稱為祖。

translations.literal: The posthumous-title deliberation also stated: "When emperors' achievements are grand and flourishing, they may invoke the ancient meaning 'the ancestor has merit' and be styled ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous-title deliberation also stated: "When emperors' achievements are grand and flourishing, they may invoke the ancient meaning 'the ancestor has merit' and be styled ancestor.

sentences.zh: 竊謂唯聖可揚峻德，唯祖可顯隆功。」

translations.literal: I venture to say only a sage can exalt towering virtue; only an ancestor can display meritorious achievement."
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say only a sage can exalt towering virtue; only an ancestor can display meritorious achievement."

sentences.zh: 議上，稱旨。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, it accorded with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, it met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 雍正初元，遂上尊諡，廟號聖祖。

translations.literal: In the inaugural year of Yongzheng, honorific posthumous titles were accordingly conferred, with the temple name Shengzu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, honorific posthumous titles were accordingly conferred, with the temple name Shengzu.

sentences.zh: 復諭：「太祖、太宗、世祖三聖相承，功高德盛；

translations.literal: He further instructed: "Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu—the three sages succeeded one another, their merit high and virtue abundant;
translations.idiomatic: He further instructed: "Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu—the three sages succeeded one another, their merit high and virtue abundant;

sentences.zh: 孝庄、孝康、孝惠翼運啟期，懿徽流慶；

translations.literal: Xiaozhuang, Xiaokang, and Xiaohui aided Heaven's mandate and opened the age, their virtue flowing in blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang, Xiaokang, and Xiaohui aided Heaven's mandate and opened the age, their virtue flowing in blessing;

sentences.zh: 宜並加諡，俾展孝思。」

translations.literal: They should all receive additional posthumous titles, that filial devotion may be expressed."
translations.idiomatic: They should all receive additional posthumous titles, that filial devotion may be expressed."

sentences.zh: 於是加諡太祖曰端毅，太宗曰敬敏，世祖曰定統建極，而孝慈、孝端及三後並尊諡焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taizu was given the additional title Duanyi, Taizong Jingmin, Shizu Dingtong Jianji, and Xiaoci, Xiaoduan, and the three empresses all received honorific posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Taizu was given the additional title Duanyi, Taizong Jingmin, Shizu Dingtong Jianji, and Xiaoci, Xiaoduan, and the three empresses all received honorific posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 於時工部奉神主廟室，魨漆飾金，中書、翰林官各一人書新諡。

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Works prepared spirit tablets for the temple chambers, lacquered with fish-bladder varnish and gilded; one official each from the Secretariat and Hanlin Academy inscribed the new posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ministry of Works prepared spirit tablets for the temple chambers, lacquered with fish-bladder varnish and gilded; one official each from the Secretariat and Hanlin Academy inscribed the new posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 奏遣大學士二人行填青禮，先期祗告天地、社稷。

translations.literal: It was memorialized that two grand secretaries be dispatched to perform the blue-inlay rite, with announcement beforehand to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: It was memorialized that two grand secretaries be dispatched to perform the blue-inlay rite, with announcement beforehand to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 至日，世宗禮服詣太廟行上尊諡禮。

translations.literal: On the day, Shizong in sacrificial robes proceeded to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the rite of conferring honorific posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, Shizong in sacrificial robes proceeded to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the rite of conferring honorific posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 畢，還宮，易袞服，詣奉先殿致祭，後仿此。

translations.literal: When complete, he returned to the palace, changed into sacrificial robes, and proceeded to Fengxian Hall to offer sacrifice—later cases followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: When complete, he returned to the palace, changed into sacrificial robes, and proceeded to Fengxian Hall to offer sacrifice—later cases followed this model.

sentences.zh: 六年，鐫造列聖、列後玉寶、玉冊暨聖祖皇考、妣冊、寶成，奉之太廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, jade seals and jade books for successive emperors and empresses, and books and seals for Shengzu's imperial father and mother, were carved and completed, and presented to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, jade seals and jade books for successive emperors and empresses, and books and seals for Shengzu's imperial father and mother, were carved and completed, and presented to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 其儀，太廟潔室設黃案，張采幔兩旁，中陳冊、寶，王大臣朝服將事，帝御禮服恭閱，一跪三拜，安奉采亭，輿導如前儀。

translations.literal: The rite: in the purification chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple a yellow table was set, colored curtains hung on both sides, books and seals placed in the center; princes and ministers in court dress conducted the affair; the Emperor in sacrificial robes reverently reviewed them, one kneeling and three kowtows, then they were placed in the ceremonial pavilion and borne in procession as in the previous rite.
translations.idiomatic: The rite: in the purification chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple a yellow table was set, colored curtains hung on both sides, books and seals placed in the center; princes and ministers in court dress conducted the affair; the Emperor in sacrificial robes reverently reviewed them, one kneeling and three kowtows, then they were placed in the ceremonial pavilion and borne in procession as in the previous rite.

sentences.zh: 供案訖，帝入行禮如初。

translations.literal: When the offering tables were ready, the Emperor entered and performed the rites as at first.
translations.idiomatic: When the offering tables were ready, the Emperor entered and performed the rites as at first.

sentences.zh: 冊、寶集中殿，分藏金匱。

translations.literal: The books and seals were gathered in the central hall and separately stored in gold caskets.
translations.idiomatic: The books and seals were gathered in the central hall and separately stored in gold caskets.

sentences.zh: 帝以次上香，一跪三拜，禮成。

translations.literal: The Emperor offered incense in sequence, one kneeling and three kowtows; the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor offered incense in sequence, one kneeling and three kowtows; the rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，加列聖、列後尊諡，諭言：「宗廟徽稱有制，報本忱悃靡窮。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he added honorific posthumous titles for successive emperors and empresses, instructing: "The ancestral temple's honorific designations are regulated; gratitude to origins and sincere devotion are boundless.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he added honorific posthumous titles for successive emperors and empresses, instructing: "The ancestral temple's honorific designations are regulated; gratitude to origins and sincere devotion are boundless.

sentences.zh: 藉抒至情，不為恆式。」

translations.literal: This is to express utmost feeling, not to serve as a fixed precedent."
translations.idiomatic: This is to express utmost feeling, not to serve as a fixed precedent."

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年，以列朝冊、寶玉色參差，命選工琢和闐精璆。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, because the jade color of successive dynasties' books and seals was uneven, skilled artisans were ordered to carve fine Khotan jade.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 45, because the jade color of successive dynasties' books and seals was uneven, skilled artisans were ordered to carve fine Khotan jade.

sentences.zh: 越二年工竣，祗閱訖，奉太廟如禮。

translations.literal: Two years later the work was completed; after reverent review, they were presented to the Imperial Ancestral Temple according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the work was completed; after reverent review, they were presented to the Imperial Ancestral Temple according to rite.

sentences.zh: 其舊藏十六分，命賚送盛京太廟，尊藏玉檢金繩。

translations.literal: The former sixteen sets in storage were ordered sent as gifts to the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Mukden, reverently stored in jade caskets bound with gold cord.
translations.idiomatic: The former sixteen sets in storage were ordered sent as gifts to the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Mukden, reverently stored in jade caskets bound with gold cord.

sentences.zh: 自是帝、後祔廟，皆別備冊、寶送盛京，永為制。

translations.literal: Henceforth when emperors and empresses were enshrined in the temple, separate books and seals were prepared and sent to Mukden—a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when emperors and empresses were installed in the ancestral temple, separate books and seals were prepared and sent to Mukden—a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗守遺訓，著制，凡列聖尊諡已加至二十四字、列後尊諡已加至十六字不復議加。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, Renzong observing his predecessor's instruction established a regulation: for successive emperors, when honorific posthumous titles had already been extended to twenty-four characters, and for successive empresses to sixteen characters, no further additions would be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, Renzong observing his predecessor's instruction established a regulation: for successive emperors, when honorific posthumous titles had already reached twenty-four characters, and for successive empresses sixteen characters, no further additions would be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 功臣配饗，所以顯功，宗親郡王配東廡，文武大臣配西廡。

translations.literal: Collateral worship for meritorious ministers was to display merit: clansmen and princes of the commandery were worshipped collaterally in the east cloister, civil and military ministers in the west cloister.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral worship for meritorious ministers was to display merit: clansmen and commandery princes were worshipped collaterally in the east cloister, civil and military ministers in the west cloister.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，追封皇伯祖禮敦巴圖魯為武功郡王，巴圖魯其名也，配東廡，福晉與焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, the imperial grand-uncle Lidun Batulu was posthumously ennobled Prince of Wugong; Batulu was his name; he was given collateral worship in the east cloister, and his consort was included.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1, the imperial grand-uncle Lidun Batulu was posthumously ennobled Prince of Wugong; Batulu was his name; he was given collateral worship in the east cloister, and his consort was included.

sentences.zh: 並以直義公費英東、弘毅公額亦都配西廡。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhiyi Feiyingdong and Duke of Hongyi Eidu were also given collateral worship in the west cloister.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhiyi Feiyingdong and Duke of Hongyi Eidu were also given collateral worship in the west cloister.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，西廡增祀武勛王揚古利，位直義上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Prince of Wuxun Yangguli was added to worship in the west cloister, his place above Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, Prince of Wuxun Yangguli was added to worship in the west cloister, his place above Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 九年，復增祀忠義公圖爾格、昭勛公圖賴，昭勛為直義子，忠義為弘毅子，父子配侑，世尤榮之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Duke of Zhongyi Turgene and Duke of Zhaoxun Tulai were again added; Zhaoxun was Zhiyi's son, Zhongyi was Eidu's son—father and son worshipped collaterally, an honor especially glorious in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Duke of Zhongyi Turgene and Duke of Zhaoxun Tulai were again added; Zhaoxun was Zhiyi's son, Zhongyi was Eidu's son—father and son worshipped collaterally, an honor especially glorious in the age.

sentences.zh: 十一年，東廡增祀通達郡王雅爾哈齊、慧哲郡王額爾袞、宣獻郡王界堪，通達位武功上，而慧哲、宣獻兩福晉亦並侑雲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Prince of Tongda Yarhaqi, Prince of Huizhe Ejeren, and Prince of Xuanxian Jeken were added to the east cloister; Tongda's place was above Wugong, and the consorts of Huizhe and Xuanxian were also joined in collateral worship.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Prince of Tongda Yarhaqi, Prince of Huizhe Ejeren, and Prince of Xuanxian Jeken were added to the east cloister; Tongda's place was above Wugong, and the consorts of Huizhe and Xuanxian were also joined in collateral worship.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，定祀東廡用太牢，歲以為常。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, it was fixed that worship in the east cloister use the great offering, annually as a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9, it was fixed that worship in the east cloister use the great offering, annually as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，西廡增祀文襄公圖海。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, Duke of Wenxiang Tu Hai was added to worship in the west cloister.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, Duke of Wenxiang Tu Hai was added to worship in the west cloister.

sentences.zh: 定功臣配饗儀，前期告太廟。

translations.literal: The rite for meritorious ministers' collateral worship was fixed: the Imperial Ancestral Temple was notified beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The rite for meritorious ministers' collateral worship was fixed: the Imperial Ancestral Temple was notified beforehand.

sentences.zh: 屆日陳采亭，列引仗，奉主至廟西階。

translations.literal: On the appointed day the ceremonial pavilion was set out, honor guard arrayed, and the tablet borne to the west steps of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the ceremonial pavilion was set out, honor guard arrayed, and the tablet borne to the west steps of the temple.

sentences.zh: 拜位在階下，三跪九拜。

translations.literal: The place of obeisance was below the steps: three kneelings and nine kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The place of obeisance was below the steps: three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 奉主大臣攝行，還納龕位，一跪三拜。

translations.literal: The minister bearing the tablet performed the rite by proxy; returning, the tablet was placed in the niche, with one kneeling and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: The minister bearing the tablet performed the rite by proxy; returning, the tablet was placed in the niche, with one kneeling and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 八年，怡親王允祥配東廡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Prince Yi Yinxiang was given collateral worship in the east cloister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Prince Yi Yinxiang was given collateral worship in the east cloister.

sentences.zh: 定王配饗儀，奉主以郡王，迎主用采亭吾仗，至廟東階，拜位在階上。

translations.literal: The rite for princes' collateral worship was fixed: the tablet was borne by a commandery prince; to receive the tablet a ceremonial pavilion and guard of honor were used; reaching the east steps of the temple, the place of obeisance was on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The rite for princes' collateral worship was fixed: the tablet was borne by a commandery prince; to receive the tablet a ceremonial pavilion and guard of honor were used; reaching the east steps of the temple, the place of obeisance was on the steps.

sentences.zh: 代行禮畢，降自東階，餘如西廡。

translations.literal: When the proxy rites were complete, he descended the east steps; the remainder followed the west cloister.
translations.idiomatic: When the proxy rites were complete, he descended the east steps; the remainder followed the west cloister.

sentences.zh: 九年，進加費英東信勇公，圖爾格果毅公，圖賴雄勇公，圖海忠達公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Feiyingdong was promoted to Duke of Xinyong, Turgene to Duke of Guoyi, Tulai to Duke of Xiongyong, and Tu Hai to Duke of Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Feiyingdong was promoted to Duke of Xinyong, Turgene to Duke of Guoyi, Tulai to Duke of Xiongyong, and Tu Hai to Duke of Zhongda.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，西廡增祀襄勤伯鄂爾泰，超勇親王策凌，大學士張廷玉，蒙古王、漢大臣侑食自此始。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, the west cloister added Duke of Xiangqin Ortai, Prince of Chaoyong Čering, and Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu—Mongol princes and Han ministers in collateral feasting began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign, the west cloister added Duke of Xiangqin Ortai, Prince of Chaoyong Čering, and Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu—Mongol princes and Han ministers in collateral feasting began from this.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，詔：「祖宗創業艱難，懿親藎臣，佐命殊功，從古未有。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, an edict stated: "Our forebears' founding of the enterprise was arduous; worthy kinsmen and devoted ministers aided the mandate with extraordinary merit such as antiquity never knew.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, an edict stated: "Our forebears' founding of the enterprise was arduous; worthy kinsmen and devoted ministers aided the mandate with extraordinary merit such as antiquity never knew.

sentences.zh: 當時崇封錫爵，酬答從優。

translations.literal: At the time they were richly ennobled and granted titles, rewarded with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were richly ennobled and granted titles, rewarded with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 以後有及身緣事降削者，有子孫承襲易封者，不為追復舊恩，心實未愜。」

translations.literal: Later some suffered reduction or deprivation in their lifetimes for cause; some whose descendants inherited had their titles changed—without restoring the old grace, the heart was truly unsatisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Later some suffered reduction or deprivation in their lifetimes for cause; some whose descendants inherited had their titles changed—without restoring the old grace, the heart was truly unsatisfied."

sentences.zh: 於是睿親王多爾袞以元勛懿戚，橫被流言，特旨昭雪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Rui Dorgon, as founding minister and imperial kinsman, had been wronged by slander; a special edict cleared his name.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Rui Dorgon, as founding minister and imperial kinsman, had been wronged by slander; a special edict cleared his name.

sentences.zh: 禮烈親王代善，後人改封為巽，已復改為康，鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗改為簡，豫通親王多鐸改為信，肅裕親王豪格改為顯，克勤郡王岳託改為衍禧，又改為平，均非初號。

translations.literal: Prince Li Daišan, whose descendants later changed his title to Xun, then again to Kang; Prince of Zhengxian Jirhalang changed to Jian; Prince of Yutong Dodo changed to Xin; Prince of Suyu Hooge changed to Xian; Prince of Keqin Yoto changed to Yanxi, then again to Ping—all differed from the original designations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Daišan, whose descendants later changed his title to Xun, then again to Kang; Prince of Zhengxian Jirhalang changed to Jian; Prince of Yutong Dodo changed to Xin; Prince of Suyu Hooge changed to Xian; Prince of Keqin Yoto changed to Yanxi, then again to Ping—all differed from the original designations.

sentences.zh: 悉命復舊，並配祀東廡。

translations.literal: All were ordered restored to the old titles and given collateral sacrifice in the east cloister.
translations.idiomatic: All were ordered restored to the old titles and given collateral sacrifice in the east cloister.

sentences.zh: 禮王位宣獻下，睿王等以次列序，位怡王上，而徙策凌列怡王次。

translations.literal: Prince Li's place was below Xuanxian; Prince Rui and the others were arranged in order below him, above Prince Yi; and Čering was moved to follow Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li's place was below Xuanxian; Prince Rui and the others were arranged in order below him, above Prince Yi; and Čering was moved to follow Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，西廡增大學士傅恆、福康安、協辦大學士兆惠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, the west cloister added Grand Secretaries Fu Heng and Fukang'an, and Associate Grand Secretary Zhaohui.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, the west cloister added Grand Secretaries Fu Heng and Fukang'an, and Associate Grand Secretary Zhaohui.

sentences.zh: 福康安即傅恆子，並封郡王，異姓世臣，被恩最渥。

translations.literal: Fukang'an was Fu Heng's son; both were ennobled as commandery princes—non-imperial clansmen who served for generations, receiving grace beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an was Fu Heng's son; both were ennobled as commandery princes—non-imperial clansmen who served for generations, receiving grace beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，復增大學士阿桂，功臣凡十有二人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, Grand Secretary Agui was again added; meritorious ministers totaled twelve persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3, Grand Secretary Agui was again added; meritorious ministers totaled twelve persons.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，東廡增科爾沁親王僧格林沁，功王凡十有三人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, Prince of Horqin Sengge Rinchen was added to the east cloister; meritorious princes totaled thirteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4, Prince of Horqin Sengge Rinchen was added to the east cloister; meritorious princes totaled thirteen persons.

sentences.zh: 凡時饗，帝上香時，分獻官上香配位前，各分獻不拜。

translations.literal: At seasonal offerings, when the Emperor offered incense, collateral presentation officers offered incense before the collateral places; each presented separately without obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: At seasonal offerings, when the Emperor offered incense, collateral presentation officers offered incense before the collateral places; each presented separately without obeisance.

sentences.zh: 三獻畢，退。

translations.literal: When the three presentations were complete, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the three presentations were complete, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 祫祭同。

translations.literal: The same applied to collective ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to collective ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王廟光緒十六年，醇賢親王奕枻薨，中旨引高宗濮議辨，應稱所生曰「本生父」，沒稱「本生考」，立廟不祧，祀以天子之禮，合乎「父為士，子為大夫，葬以士，祭以大夫」古義，斯尊親兩全矣。

translations.literal: Temple of the Worthy and Virtuous Prince Chun. In the sixteenth year of Guangxu, Prince Chun the Worthy and Virtuous Yixuan died; an imperial instruction cited Gaozong's analysis of the Tang succession controversy, holding that one's biological forebear should in life be styled "biological father" and after death "deceased biological father"; a temple was established without displacement from the line, worshipped with the rites of a Son of Heaven—consistent with the ancient meaning "the father was a shi, the son a grandee: bury as a shi, sacrifice as a grandee"—thus honoring kin while fulfilling both obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Temple of the Worthy and Virtuous Prince Chun. In Guangxu 16, Prince Chun the Worthy and Virtuous Yixuan died; an imperial instruction cited Gaozong's analysis of the Tang succession controversy, holding that one's biological forebear should in life be styled "biological father" and after death "deceased biological father"; a temple was established without displacement from the line, worshipped with the rites of a Son of Heaven—consistent with the ancient meaning "the father was a shi, the son a grandee: bury as a shi, sacrifice as a grandee"—thus honoring kin while fulfilling both obligations.

sentences.zh: 乃定稱號曰「皇帝本生考」。

translations.literal: The style and title were then fixed as "Deceased Biological Father the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The style and title were then fixed as "Deceased Biological Father the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 復定廟祀典，建廟新賜邸第，額曰醇賢親王廟。

translations.literal: The temple sacrifice code was also fixed; a temple was built at the newly granted residence, its plaque reading Temple of the Worthy and Virtuous Prince Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The temple sacrifice code was also fixed; a temple was built at the newly granted residence, its plaque reading Temple of the Worthy and Virtuous Prince Chun.

sentences.zh: 正殿七楹，東、西廡殿，後寢室，各五楹。

translations.literal: The main hall had seven bays; east and west side halls and rear sleeping chambers each had five bays.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had seven bays; east and west side halls and rear sleeping chambers each had five bays.

sentences.zh: 中門三。

translations.literal: The central gate had three openings.
translations.idiomatic: The central gate had three openings.

sentences.zh: 門內焚帛亭、祭器亭，其外宰牲亭、神庫、神廚。

translations.literal: Within the gate were pavilions for burning silks and for sacrificial vessels; outside were the slaughter pavilion, spirit storehouse, and spirit kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Within the gate were pavilions for burning silks and for sacrificial vessels; outside were the slaughter pavilion, spirit storehouse, and spirit kitchen.

sentences.zh: 大門三。

translations.literal: The great gate had three openings.
translations.idiomatic: The great gate had three openings.

sentences.zh: 殿宇正門中覆黃琉璃，殿脊及門四周上覆綠琉璃。

translations.literal: On the main hall's central gate yellow glazed tile was used; on the hall ridge and all around the gates green glazed tile covered the upper portions.
translations.idiomatic: On the main hall's central gate yellow glazed tile was used; on the hall ridge and all around the gates green glazed tile covered the upper portions.

sentences.zh: 其祀儀、樂舞、祭器、祭品視天子禮。

translations.literal: Sacrificial rites, music and dance, vessels, and offerings followed the Son of Heaven's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial rites, music and dance, vessels, and offerings followed the Son of Heaven's rites.

sentences.zh: 凡時饗以四仲月朔，襲王承祭。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings fell on the first day of each of the four mid-season months; the title heir prince presided over sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings fell on the first day of each of the four mid-season months; the title heir prince presided over sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝親行，則襲王陪祀。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed the rite in person, the title heir prince attended as collaterally worshipping aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor performed the rite in person, the title heir prince attended as collaterally worshipping aide.

sentences.zh: 誕辰、忌日，帝親詣行禮。

translations.literal: On birthdays and death anniversaries, the Emperor personally proceeded to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On birthdays and death anniversaries, the Emperor personally proceeded to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 謁陵有清肇跡興京，四祖陵並在京西北，稱興京陵。

translations.literal: Imperial tomb visits: Qing's founding traces lie at Xingjing; the tombs of the Four Ancestors together lie northwest of the capital, called the Xingjing tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tomb visits: the Qing founding traces lie at Xingjing; the tombs of the Four Ancestors together lie northwest of the capital, called the Xingjing tombs.

sentences.zh: 太祖定遼陽，景祖、顯祖二陵徙盛京東南，稱東京陵。

translations.literal: After Taizu pacified Liaoyang, the tombs of Jingzu and Xianzu were moved southeast of Mukden, called the Eastern Capital tombs.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu pacified Liaoyang, the tombs of Jingzu and Xianzu were moved southeast of Mukden, called the Eastern Capital tombs.

sentences.zh: 嗣是太祖陵當盛京東北，稱福陵；

translations.literal: Thereafter Taizu's tomb lay northeast of Mukden, called Fuling;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Taizu's tomb lay northeast of Mukden, called Fuling;

sentences.zh: 太宗陵當盛京西北，稱昭陵。

translations.literal: Taizong's tomb lay northwest of Mukden, called Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's tomb lay northwest of Mukden, called Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，定歲暮、清明祭興京陵，用牛一，遣守陵官行禮。

translations.literal: In the Chongde period it was fixed that at year's end and Qingming the Xingjing tombs be sacrificed to with one ox; tomb-keeping officials were dispatched to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongde period it was fixed that at year's end and Qingming the Xingjing tombs be sacrificed to with one ox; tomb-keeping officials were dispatched to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 東京陵用牛二，遣宗室、覺羅大臣行禮。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital tombs used two oxen; Banner nobles and imperial clansmen ministers were dispatched to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital tombs used two oxen; Banner nobles and imperial clansmen ministers were dispatched to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 福陵用牛一、羊二，遣大臣行禮。

translations.literal: Fuling used one ox and two sheep; ministers were dispatched to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling used one ox and two sheep; ministers were dispatched to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 國忌、誕辰、孟秋望日，燃香燭，獻酒果，奠帛、讀祝、行禮。

translations.literal: On death anniversaries, birthdays, and the full moon of the first autumn month, incense and candles were lit, wine and fruit presented, silks laid, prayers read, and rites performed.
translations.idiomatic: On death anniversaries, birthdays, and the full moon of the seventh month, incense and candles were lit, wine and fruit presented, silks laid, prayers read, and rites performed.

sentences.zh: 朔、望用牛一，具香燭、酒果，遣守陵官致祭，不讀祝、奠帛。

translations.literal: On new and full moon days one ox was used, with incense, candles, and wine and fruit; tomb-keeping officials were dispatched to sacrifice, without reading prayers or laying silks.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moon days one ox was used, with incense, candles, and wine and fruit; tomb-keeping officials were dispatched to sacrifice, without reading prayers or laying silks.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，封興京陵山曰啟運，東京陵山曰積慶，福陵山曰天柱，昭陵山曰隆業，並從祀方澤，置陵官、陵戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, the Xingjing tomb mountain was titled Qiyun, the Eastern Capital tomb mountain Jiqing, the Fuling mountain Tianzhu, and the Zhaoling mountain Longye; all were given collateral worship at the Altar of Earth, and tomb officials and tomb households were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8, the Xingjing tomb mountain was titled Qiyun, the Eastern Capital tomb mountain Jiqing, the Fuling mountain Tianzhu, and the Zhaoling mountain Longye; all were given collateral worship at the Altar of Earth, and tomb officials and tomb households were established.

sentences.zh: 定祀儀，冬至用牛一、羊一、豕一，餘同前。

translations.literal: Sacrificial rites were fixed: at the winter solstice one ox, one sheep, and one pig were used; the remainder followed the previous model.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial rites were fixed: at the winter solstice one ox, one sheep, and one pig were used; the remainder followed the previous model.

sentences.zh: 清明、歲暮、孟秋望日亦如之。

translations.literal: Qingming, year's end, and the full moon of the first autumn month were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Qingming, year's end, and the full moon of the seventh month were the same.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔立界碑，禁樵採。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict ordered boundary steles erected and woodcutting forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, an edict ordered boundary steles erected and woodcutting forbidden.

sentences.zh: 十五年，移東京陵改祔興京，罷積慶山祀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the Eastern Capital tombs were moved and enshrined at Xingjing instead; sacrifice at Jiqing Mountain was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, the Eastern Capital tombs were moved and retroactively enshrined at Xingjing, and sacrifice at Jiqing Mountain was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 明年，尊稱為永陵，饗殿、暖閣如制。

translations.literal: The following year, it was honored with the title Yongling; the sacrifice hall and warm chamber followed the prescribed model.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, it was honored with the title Yongling; the sacrifice hall and warm chamber were built according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，相度遵化鳳台山建世祖陵，曰孝陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, a site was surveyed on Fengtai Mountain in Zunhua to build Shizu's tomb, called Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2, a site was surveyed on Fengtai Mountain in Zunhua to build Shizu's tomb, called Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 先是世祖校獵於此，停轡四顧曰：「此山王氣蔥鬱，可為朕壽宮。」

translations.literal: Earlier Shizu had hunted here; reining in his horse he looked about and said: "This mountain's royal qi is lush and dense—it may serve as my tomb palace."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while hunting here, Shizu reined in his horse, looked about, and said: "This mountain's royal aura is dense and auspicious—it will serve as my tomb."

sentences.zh: 因自取佩鞢擲之，諭侍臣曰：「鞢落處定為穴。」

translations.literal: He then took his own worn scabbard-chape and threw it, instructing attendant officials: "Where the chape falls shall be fixed as the tomb site."
translations.idiomatic: He then took the worn chape from his own scabbard and threw it, telling his attendants: "Where the chape falls shall be the tomb site."

sentences.zh: 至是陵成，皆驚為吉壤。

translations.literal: When the tomb was complete at this point, all marveled that it was an auspicious site.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was completed, all marveled that it was an auspicious site.

sentences.zh: 歲以清明、中元、冬至、歲暮為四大祭。

translations.literal: Each year Qingming, Zhongyuan, the winter solstice, and year's end were fixed as the four great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Qingming, Zhongyuan, the winter solstice, and year's end were established as the four great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 並改建福陵、昭陵地宮。

translations.literal: Fuling and Zhaoling underground chambers were also rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: The underground chambers of Fuling and Zhaoling were also rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 工竣，以奉安祗告，致祭如大饗。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, an announcement was made for the installation; sacrifice was performed as at a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, an announcement was made for the installation; sacrifice was performed as at a great feast.

sentences.zh: 安神位隆恩殿，制龕座、寶床、帷幔、衾褥、楎椸如太廟式。

translations.literal: The spirit seat was installed in Long'en Hall; niche, precious couch, curtains, bedding, and clothing racks were made after the Great Temple model.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seat was installed in Long'en Hall; niche, precious couch, curtains, bedding, and clothing racks were made after the model of the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 凡因公謁陵，三品以上官羅城門外行禮。

translations.literal: Whenever one visited tombs on official business, officials of third rank and above performed rites outside the outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one visited the tombs on official business, officials of third rank and above performed rites outside the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 遇祭日，二品以上許入城隨守陵官陪祭。

translations.literal: On sacrifice days, those of second rank and above were permitted to enter the enclosure and join tomb-keeping officials in collateral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On sacrifice days, officials of second rank and above were permitted to enter the enclosure and join tomb-keeping officials in collateral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 歸，謁辭。

translations.literal: On departure, a farewell visit was made.
translations.idiomatic: On departure, a farewell visit was made.

sentences.zh: 凡謁陵，東逕石門，王、貝勒在隆恩門外三跪九拜，當直官啟門，貝子以下、三品官以上則否，皆奉祀官為導，遇祭日免。

translations.literal: Whenever visiting tombs, one went east through Shimen; princes and beile prostrated three times and bowed nine times outside Long'en Gate; the duty officer opened the gate—for lesser princes through third-rank officials, no—sacrifice officials served as guides; waived on sacrifice days.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting the tombs, one went east through Shimen; princes and beile performed three kneelings and nine kowtows outside Long'en Gate, and the duty officer opened the gate. For imperial princes of lesser rank through officials of third rank and above, the gate was not opened; sacrifice officials served as guides—except on sacrifice days.

sentences.zh: 是時三陵建功德碑，嗣凡起陵，皆立碑，如故事。

translations.literal: At this time merit steles were erected at the three tombs; thereafter whenever a tomb was built, a stele was erected, following precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At this time merit steles were erected at the three tombs; thereafter, whenever a tomb was established, a stele was erected, following precedent.

sentences.zh: 八年，定四時大祭，遣多羅貝勒以下，奉國將軍、覺羅男以上行禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the four seasonal great sacrifices were fixed; those dispatched ranged from duo-luo beile down and from fengguo jiangjun and jueluo nan up to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the four seasonal great sacrifices were fixed; those dispatched to perform the rites ranged from duo-luo beile downward and from fengguo jiangjun and jueluo nan upward.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，奉太皇太后、皇太后率皇后謁孝陵。

translations.literal: The following autumn, the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager led the empress to visit Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn, led by the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager, the empress visited Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 前一日，躬告太廟，越日啟鑾。

translations.literal: The day before, in person an announcement was made at the Great Temple; the next day the imperial procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Emperor in person announced at the Great Temple; the next day the imperial procession set out.

sentences.zh: 陳鹵簿，不作樂。

translations.literal: The imperial guard of honor was arrayed; no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial guard of honor was arrayed; no music was performed.

sentences.zh: 既達陵所，太皇太后坐方城東旁，奠酒舉哀。

translations.literal: Having reached the tomb precinct, the Grand Empress Dowager sat at the east side of the square enclosure, poured wine, and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Having reached the tomb precinct, the Grand Empress Dowager sat at the east side of the square enclosure, poured wine, and wailed.

sentences.zh: 皇太后率皇后等詣明樓前中立，六肅、三跪、三拜，隨舉哀、奠酒，復三拜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager led the empress and others to stand before Minglou; six rounds of solemnity, three kneelings, three bows; wine was poured amid wailing, then three bows again.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager led the empress and others to stand before Minglou; six rounds of solemnity, three kneelings, and three bows; amid wailing they poured wine, then bowed three times again.

sentences.zh: 還行宮。

translations.literal: They returned to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 凡皇太后謁陵仿此。

translations.literal: Whenever an empress dowager visited tombs, it followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an empress dowager visited the tombs, the rites followed this model.

sentences.zh: 次日，帝復謁隆恩殿，行大饗禮。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor again visited Long'en Hall and performed the great feast rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor again visited Long'en Hall and performed the great feast rites.

sentences.zh: 又次日，殿前設黃幄，焚楮帛，讀文致祭，禮成。

translations.literal: On the day after that, a yellow canopy was set before the hall; paper silks were burned, a text read, and sacrifice performed—the rites complete.
translations.idiomatic: On the day after that, a yellow canopy was set before the hall; paper silks were burned, a text was read, and sacrifice was performed—the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 還京，仍告太廟。

translations.literal: On return to the capital, announcement was again made at the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On return to the capital, announcement was again made at the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 越二日，御太和殿，百官表賀。

translations.literal: Two days later, he presided over the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the hundred officials presented congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, he presided over the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the hundred officials presented congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，車駕至盛京，謁福陵、昭陵畢，召將軍等賜以酒，並諭守陵總管、副總管曰：「爾等職司典祀，凡祭品必親虔視，務盡誠敬，副朕孝思。」

translations.literal: The following autumn the imperial carriage reached Mukden; after visiting Fuling and Zhaoling, generals and others were summoned and given wine, and the tomb-keeping chief and deputy chief were instructed: "Your offices supervise the canonical sacrifices; for all sacrificial offerings you must personally and reverently inspect them, striving for utmost sincerity and respect, assisting my filial thoughts."
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the imperial carriage reached Mukden; after visiting Fuling and Zhaoling, generals and others were summoned and given wine, and the chief and deputy tomb-keepers were instructed: "Your offices supervise the canonical sacrifices; you must personally and reverently inspect all sacrificial offerings, striving for utmost sincerity and respect, assisting my filial devotion."

sentences.zh: 還御大清門受賀，燕賚群臣，頒守陵官軍。

translations.literal: On return he presided at Daqing Gate to receive congratulations, feasted and rewarded the ministers, and distributed rewards to tomb-keeping officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On return he presided at Daqing Gate to receive congratulations, feasted and rewarded the ministers, and distributed rewards to tomb-keeping officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其永陵遣王大臣致祭，復遣官分詣穎親王、克勤郡王、直義公費英東諸勛貴墓酹酒。

translations.literal: At Yongling a prince or minister was dispatched to sacrifice; officials were also dispatched separately to pour libations at the tombs of Prince Ying, Prince Keqin, and the Honorary Righteous Duke Fei Yingdong and other meritorious nobles.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongling a prince or minister was dispatched to sacrifice; officials were also dispatched separately to pour libations at the tombs of Prince Ying, Prince Keqin, the Honorary Righteous Duke Fei Yingdong, and other meritorious nobles.

sentences.zh: 還京日，仍告廟如儀。

translations.literal: On the day of return to the capital, announcement was still made at the temple according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of return to the capital, announcement was still made at the temple according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，滇平，詣兩京謁陵，如初禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Yunnan was pacified; tombs in both capitals were visited, as at the initial rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, after Yunnan was pacified, the tombs in both capitals were visited, as at the initial rites.

sentences.zh: 還京，祗告奉先殿。

translations.literal: On return to the capital, reverent announcement was made at the Hall of Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: On return to the capital, reverent announcement was made at the Hall of Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 自是靖寇難，謁陵告祭以為常。

translations.literal: From this, whenever bandit troubles were pacified, tomb visits and announcement sacrifices became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever bandit troubles were pacified, tomb visits and announcement sacrifices became the norm.

sentences.zh: 六十年，御極周甲，命世宗率皇子、皇孫詣盛京，皇子祭昭陵，皇孫祭永陵，帝親往福陵大祭。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, at the completion of a sexagenary cycle on the throne, Shizong was ordered to lead princes and imperial grandsons to Mukden; a prince sacrificed at Zhaoling, an imperial grandson at Yongling; the Emperor personally went to Fuling for a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, at the completion of a sexagenary cycle on the throne, Shizong was ordered to lead princes and imperial grandsons to Mukden; a prince sacrificed at Zhaoling, an imperial grandson at Yongling; the Emperor personally went to Fuling for a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，定聖祖陵曰景陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Shengzu's tomb was fixed as Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, Shengzu's tomb was officially named Jingling.

sentences.zh: 其明年，清明謁祭如典。

translations.literal: The following year, Qingming tomb visit and sacrifice followed the canon.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the Qingming tomb visit and sacrifice followed the canon.

sentences.zh: 八年冬至，會聖祖忌辰，禮臣言准陵寢大祭，用太牢，獻帛、爵，讀祝文。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice of the eighth year, coinciding with Shengzu's death anniversary, ritual officials said to approve a great sacrifice at the tomb precinct, using the grand offering; silks and cups were presented and the prayer text read.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice of the eighth year, coinciding with Shengzu's death anniversary, ritual officials recommended approving a great sacrifice at the tomb precinct, using the grand offering; silks and cups were presented and the prayer text was read.

sentences.zh: 遣官承祭具朝服。

translations.literal: An official was dispatched to receive and sacrifice, fully attired in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: An official was dispatched to preside at the sacrifice, fully attired in court dress.

sentences.zh: 十三年清明、冬至大饗，改遣公爵番行。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, at Qingming and winter solstice great feasts, dispatch was changed to dukes in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, at the Qingming and winter solstice great feasts, dispatch was changed to dukes serving in rotation.

sentences.zh: 七月望日，將軍、侍郎等承祭，其朔、望、忌辰，則定總管掌關防承祭，行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the seventh month, generals, vice presidents, and others received and sacrificed; on new moon, full moon, and death anniversaries, the chief steward holding the seal received and sacrificed, performing three kneelings and nine kowtows.
